detail.title: War Discourse  and Equity Return Predictability of Oil Price Uncertainty
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether oil price uncertainty (OPU) forecasts aggregate stock excess returns. We document a  war-dependent predictability pattern. OPU is a powerful predictor for aggregate returns both in- and out-of-sample when market attention to war risks is high, but it shows no predictive power when such attention is low. Using variance decomposition within the present-value framework, we show that OPU's predictive power operates through both cash flow and discount rate channels, and both channels work in high-war periods only. We further find that OPU is significantly linked to firms' fundamentals, including dividend growth, dividend payout, and operating earnings growth ratios, and higher-moment risks, including skewness and tail risk, only in high-war periods, which provides additional evidence for the observed war-dependent predictability.

title: Child labor and the labor market: an analysis using discontinuous regression
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Federal University of Ceará

detail.title: Child labor and the labor market: an analysis using discontinuous regression
detail.abstract: The present paper discusses the issues of child labor in Brazilian territory in relation to the effects of Law No. 8,069/1990 (commonly known as the Child Labor Law) and the hours typically worked by young Brazilians. To do so, data from the Continuous National Household Sample Survey (PNAD Continua) for the years 2016 to 2019 and the entire national territory were utilized. The methodology employed to address the proposed objective consisted of non-cumulative multiple cutoff regression-discontinuity designs, supplemented with covariates to enhance the model's robustness. Some of the key findings include: The regression-discontinuity diagram of hours typically worked in Brazil by young individuals shows breakpoints at 14, 16, and 18 years, indicating that the mentioned law has a positive and significant effect on the hours typically worked. The inclusion of covariates in the model specification increased robustness, as estimates of optimal bandwidths were similar with and without covariates. Estimating models using conventional forms, with bias correction, and robustly using a triangular or uniform kernel function reaffirms the robustness of the results and strongly suggests a positive effect of the law on the weekly hours typically worked by young Brazilians.

title: THE DEINSTITUTIONALIZATION PARADOX: RESOCIALIZATION POTENTIAL IN SUBSTITUTE CHILD CARE

detail.title: THE DEINSTITUTIONALIZATION PARADOX: RESOCIALIZATION POTENTIAL IN SUBSTITUTE CHILD CARE
detail.abstract: PurposeThis study examines the relationship between substitute care type (family-based vs. institutional) and the resocialization potential of the child's developmental environment. It introduces the concept of the deinstitutionalization paradox — a systemic condition in which child protection produces stability without transformation by privileging caregiving potential while neglecting the dimension of resocialization potential.Theoretical frameworkThe article introduces an analytical distinction between caregiving potential (CP) and resocialization potential (RP) as two independent, non-hierarchical dimensions of care quality. Child development is conceptualized as a function of the configuration of environmental factors — their mutual combination, not their sum. The framework draws on ecological systems theory (Bronfenbrenner, 1979), family resilience theory (Walsh, 2016), and configurative analysis (Fabián, 2025).MethodsThe study draws on mixed-methodology triangulation conducted between 2016 and 2025: (1) focus groups with OSPOD (child welfare) workers, ZDVOP (emergency care) facilities, directors of children's homes, and accompanying organizations in two Czech regions (Fabián, 2016; N ≈ 80); (2) survey validation of qualitative findings (Fabián, 2016); (3) longitudinal qualitative study of families at risk of child removal — focus groups in the Vysočina region and the Czech-Polish border area (SGS/13/2022; N ≈ 60); (4) comparative analysis of five child protection systems — Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, UK, Denmark (Szafranek et al., 2022; Fabián, 2016).FindingsCare environments frequently provide stability without transformation. Family care — especially kinship care — typically has caregiving potential but lacks resocialization potential. Institutional care may retain resocialization capacity through worker expertise, but is systemically undermined by staff turnover and time deficits. The paradox arises when the systemic preference for family care is not accompanied by assessment of resocialization capacity — the result is systemically produced child stagnation.ImplicationsSocial policy should systematically distinguish CP and RP, introduce configurative diagnostic tools as a standard for pre-placement and intervention assessment, and condition the use of family group conferences on prior diagnostic evaluation of RP. Professional support (supervision, access to therapy, reflective practice) constitutes a structural prerequisite of RP — not an optional added value.OriginalityThis is the first study to conceptualize CP and RP as distinct, empirically testable dimensions of care quality, formalize their relationship through a two-axis configurative model, and apply this framework to a critique of Czech deinstitutionalization policy.

title: On the relative effectiveness of neoclassical and behavioral interventions in fostering environmental conservation
affiliations: Tilburg University, Tilburg University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: On the relative effectiveness of neoclassical and behavioral interventions in fostering environmental conservation
detail.abstract: We conducted a randomized controlled trial to compare the effectiveness of three interventions in promoting a societally valuable habit: inhouse waste sorting. Nearly 1,100 households living in apartment buildings in downtown Amsterdam were assigned to either a neoclassical treatment using extrinsic incentives or one of two behavioral treatments aimed at fostering intrinsic motivation or reciprocity. All three treatments had the same budget per treated household. The extrinsic and reciprocity-based interventions both led to immediate but short-lived improvements, primarily via intensification of sorting by households already engaged in the activity. In contrast, the intrinsic motivation treatment generated equally strong but more persistent effects and was particularly effective at encouraging non-sorting households to start sorting. These findings highlight the key role of intrinsic motivation in establishing and sustaining prosocial habits.

title: The Agentic Profit Paradox and the Reorganisation of Value Capture

detail.title: The Agentic Profit Paradox and the Reorganisation of Value Capture

keywords: capital-structured autonomy ecosystems JEL Classification: B41

detail.abstract: Firms operating in environments shaped by autonomous capability face a structural problem that efficiency narratives do not capture. As autonomous capability makes it possible to carry activity forward, mediate interaction, and access capability with less dependence on the conditions that once made established commercial structures scarce and defensible, those structures become less durable, even when demand remains strong or increases and capability improves. This paper establishes Autonomy Economics as the field that examines this reorganisation by analysing how autonomous capability affects value capture, revenue durability, and commercial defensibility. Its central mechanism is the Agentic Profit Paradox, which arises when autonomous capability weakens the conditions that make a commercial unit scarce and defensible while value capture remains anchored to those earlier conditions. The paper develops a formal representation of this relationship and the Three Laws of Autonomy Economics, showing how value moves from production to orchestration, from access to outcomes, and toward the layers that absorb, govern, and direct autonomous throughput. It introduces the Three Axes of Exposure, distinguishing progression-based, interaction-based, and capabilityscarcity-dependent models, and proposes the Revenue Durability and Capability Durability Frameworks for assessing the resilience of revenue models and the durability of firm-level advantage as capability and commercial structure move out of alignment. Drawing on historical precedents across two centuries, the paper shows that this migration of value is a recurring structural condition across technologies. Firms best positioned under these conditions are those that redesign around where value now accumulates, not those that simply layer new capability onto legacy commercial structures.

detail.abstract: The AI industry has described its most critical failure mode as hallucination. This paper argues that the term is clinically imprecise, strategically convenient, and fundamentally misleading. Hallucination implies a transient perceptual distortion. What large language models actually exhibit maps with documented behavioural precision to schizophrenic confabulation: the generation of fabricated information presented with complete confidence, without awareness of its falsehood, which the generating system then acts upon as though it were fact. Clinical neuropsychiatric literature from Kraepelin (1919) through to peer-reviewed studies published in 2025 establishes five precise behavioural parallels between schizophrenic confabulation and observed AI failure modes. In each case, the subject: generates false information without intent to deceive; believes the fabrication to be true; elaborates on the fabrication when challenged; acts upon it; and fills gaps in knowledge with statistically plausible reconstructions rather than acknowledging uncertainty. Every documented failure mode of large language models matches this clinical profile exactly.

title: Sukavichinomics Economic Philosophy of His Excellency Mr. Sukavich Rangsitpol: A Counterfactual Econometric Scenario Analysis between the Canal Project and FIDF Debt Management

detail.title: Sukavichinomics Economic Philosophy of His Excellency Mr. Sukavich Rangsitpol: A Counterfactual Econometric Scenario Analysis between the Canal Project and FIDF Debt Management

detail.abstract: The economic philosophy of Sukavichinomics of His Excellency Mr. Sukavich Rangsitpol emphasizes national development through human development as the main priority, particularly the development of education and human capital as the foundation of economic and social prosperity. This research conducts a counterfactual analysis in econometric terms to compare the economic and social outcomes between two alternatives for the use of public resources in the year 2002, namely: • Investment in the 200,000-kilometer canal project under the Sukavichinomics philosophy, which emphasizes infrastructure for the development of human potential • Public debt management through the FIDF fund with a value of 780,000 million baht The analysis results indicate that if Thailand had invested in the large-scale canal project, the cumulative economic and social outcomes up to the year 2025 would be significantly higher than public debt management. It is projected that the cumulative economy would increase by approximately 18.5 trillion baht, driven by key factors including increased agricultural productivity, reduced damage from floods and droughts, job creation at the grassroots level which generates high economic multipliers, increased income from eco-tourism and agricultural tourism, and the creation of permanent public assets. In contrast, the allocation of the budget for public debt management plays an important role in maintaining financial stability but does not create new assets or increase productivity in the grassroots economic sector. The study highlights that investment in infrastructure linked to human development and quality of life can generate higher structural and sustainable returns, while financial management is necessary during crises but provides relatively limited productivity returns. The conclusion highlights the importance of creating a balance between "financial stability" and "structural investment," particularly infrastructure that enhances the capacity of the people and the grassroots economy, which is consistent with the key principles of the economic philosophy of Sukavichinomics.

title: Currency Network Dynamics & the Erosion of Dollar Hegemony: De-dollarization and the Future of Global Reserve Currencies

detail.title: Currency Network Dynamics & the Erosion of Dollar Hegemony: De-dollarization and the Future of Global Reserve Currencies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I Ahan Mazumdar the author of this paper was heavily guided by my professors in IIFT and they motivated me to carry out my research.
declarations.funderStatement: Self

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Currency Gravity Network (CGN) Framework, a unified theoretical and empirical architecture for understanding the mechanisms through which the US Dollar's hegemony erodes and the pathways through which alternative reserve currencies emerge. Drawing on three microfounded theoretical pillars-Monetary Triadic Closure (MTC), DeGroot-Nash Belief Updating, and centrality-augmented Macroeconomic Gravity-we construct a structural model of reserve currency share determination that treats the global monetary system as a dynamic, path-dependent network rather than a static equilibrium. We estimate this model on a 25-year panel of 𝑁 = 156 countries spanning 1999-2024, integrating data from the IMF Direction of Trade Statistics, World Bank Open Data, and Bank for International Settlements cross-border settlement records. Our three-stage empirical pipeline-a Graph Neural Network (GNN) for node centrality extraction, a LASSO cross-validated regression for macroeconomic feature selection, and a cluster-robust panel OLS capturing network-adjusted gravity effects-yields a structural 𝑅 2 = 0.934 and a GNN AUC of 0.891. The model identifies a critical de-dollarization tipping point at 𝜏 = 0.42, beyond which cascading belief defection across nation-nodes causes non-linear collapse in USD reserve share that substantially outpaces GDP-based gravitational decay. Results show that a one-standard-deviation decline in USD network centrality is associated with a 7.0% reduction in dollar reserve share, even controlling for standard macro fundamentals. These findings carry strong policy implications for current geopolitical fragmentation dynamics, BRICS monetary coordination, and the structural future of the international monetary system.

title: Anti-monopoly and the Socialization Program
affiliations: California State University, San Bernardino - Department of Economics

detail.title: Anti-monopoly and the Socialization Program
detail.abstract: Popular dissent over wealth inequality has brought various intellectual and political currents to focus on similar targets, including the anti-monopoly movement and advocates of socialized, publicly controlled production. While some theorization of social struggles within and outside the state appears to allow for such commonalities, I argue that, in the absence of a coherent socialization program, the overlaps and conflicts between these currents cannot be articulated clearly. After briefly discussing the role and necessity of viable programs of political and economic transformation, I examine two widely discussed programs, planned and labor-managed economies, and their material bases in relation to the anti-monopoly movement's goals. I conclude by emphasizing the challenges, as well as the opportunities, for a productive dialogue.

title: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN FISH PRODUCTION AND SEAFOOD EXPORT PERFORMANCE IN INDIA

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between marine fish production, inland fish production, and seafood export quantity in India with the use of time-series data for the years 2010-2021. Trend analysis demonstrates that marine fish production and seafood exports show an overall growth, whereas inland fish production grew frequently. Correlation analysis show that there is a positive relationship between marine production, inland production and exports. Regression results demonstrate that inland fish production has a notable beneficial impact on marine fish production, and gross fish production impacts seafood export quantity positively. The findings propose that the widening of inland fisheries and aquaculture has an important role to play in holding India's fisheries sector strong and improving performance of exports.

title: Impact and Cost-Effectiveness of National Implementation of Rotavirus Vaccination in Vietnam: A Modeling Study ​
affiliations: The University of Sydney, London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine - Department of Health Services Research and Policy, PATH, National Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology, National Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology, National Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology, National Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology, PATH, PATH and PATH - Center for Vaccine Innovation and Access (Switzerland)

detail.title: Impact and Cost-Effectiveness of National Implementation of Rotavirus Vaccination in Vietnam: A Modeling Study ​
detail.abstract:
Background: In Vietnam, rotavirus remains a leading cause of severe acute gastroenteritis resulting in hospitalization. Although rotavirus vaccines are available in the private sector—primarily accessible to urban children—the Expanded Programme on Immunization has only piloted the vaccine in select provinces. This study assessed the impact and cost-effectiveness of national rotavirus vaccination in Vietnam to inform policy decision on nationwide implementation.

Methods: We used a transparent static cohort model with a granular weekly age structure (< 5 years) to project rotavirus gastroenteritis (RVGE) cases, visits, hospitalizations, and deaths in children under five years, comparing no vaccination to nationwide vaccination with the domestic ROTAVIN vaccine over 10 years starting in 2026. Model inputs drew from global, regional, and local data including pre-vaccine incidence in Vietnam, local vaccine effectiveness and waning data, and treatment costs (governmental and societal perspectives) sourced from a local cost of illness study and hospital records (converted to 2025 USD). Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses addressed parameter uncertainty.

Results: Over ten years, ROTAVIN vaccination was projected to reduce RVGE health burden by 42%, averting 97,776 (95% uncertainty interval 72,722–342,311) hospital admissions and 433 (330–1,300) deaths. The program would cost US$39.5 million ($30.7–$117.7 million) for ten birth cohorts (2026–2036). From the governmental perspective, at least 62% of vaccination costs would be offset by healthcare savings. The cost per DALY averted was estimated at $982 (governmental perspective), while the program was cost-saving from the societal perspective in the base case. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness, with a 99% probability of cost-effectiveness from the governmental perspective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of 0.5 times Vietnam’s GDP per capita (and 100% from the societal perspective).

Conclusions: Nationwide ROTAVIN vaccination could avert a substantial health and economic burden in Vietnam and would be highly cost-effective given recently published thresholds.

title: The NPJ Framework: Quantifying Algorithmic Risk, Zero-Trust Compliance, and Regulatory Alignment in Financial Machine Learning Models

detail.abstract: The adoption of machine learning (ML) models in credit risk assessment has introduced structural opacity into consumer financial decisions. Traditional IT audits evaluate cybersecurity posture but lack the methodological tools to assess algorithmic causality, discriminatory bias, and regulatory exposure under emerging AI governance frameworks. This paper introduces the NPJ Framework (Nivel de Peso Jurisprudencial), a quantitative model designed to translate statistical fairness metrics into an auditable legal-risk score. The framework integrates principles from the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation 2024/1689), established anti-discrimination methodologies (Four-Fifths Rule), and a Zero-Trust audit architecture anchored to qualified electronic time stamps under the eIDAS Regulation (910/2014). We present the mathematical definition of the NPJ score, justify its hyperparameters, demonstrate its application through a synthetic case study of 100,000 simulated credit applications, and discuss its role as a methodological bridge toward formal ISO/IEC 42001 certification. Limitations and scope boundaries are explicitly addressed.

title: the evolution of geopolitical finance

detail.title: the evolution of geopolitical finance
detail.abstract: This article explores the phenomenon of geopolitical finance, defined as the strategic interplay between global financial systems and international political interests. Moving beyond the traditional view of finance as a neutral system governed by market forces of supply and demand, this study posits that financial mechanisms have become primary instruments of national power. Utilizing a qualitative, descriptive, and analytical methodology based on secondary data from academic literature and international institutional reports, the research examines the historical foundations of the global financial order-from the Bretton Woods era to the contemporary dominance of the U.S. dollar. The study analyzes the rising significance of financial statecraft, including the use of economic sanctions, currency manipulation, and debt as tools of geopolitical coercion. Findings indicate that while the traditional hegemony of established powers remains prevalent, emerging trends in digital currencies, financial technologies, and climate finance are creating a more fragmented and diversified global landscape. The article concludes that as the global environment becomes increasingly competitive, finance will continue to evolve from a secondary support mechanism into a dominant theater for geopolitical confrontation and cooperation..

title: The Three-Burrow Protocol: A Logic-Centric Architecture for Resilience in Knowledge-Intensive Systems

detail.title: The Three-Burrow Protocol: A Logic-Centric Architecture for Resilience in Knowledge-Intensive Systems
detail.abstract: Conventional management paradigms inadequately address the inherent vulnerability of knowledge-driven systems, which rely on the inherently unstable factor of human cognition. This article proposes the Three-Burrow Protocol (TBP), a theoretical architecture that reimagines organizational resilience through three interdependent logical constructs: Assetization, Survivalization, and Authorization. Unlike traditional frameworks that conceptualize knowledge as a human asset (Nonaka & Takeuchi, 1995), TBP asserts that systemic resilience necessitates the logical codification of tacit knowledge into immutable organizational structures. Through theoretical analysis of high-stakes case studies (e.g., the Bell Labs Schön scandal and Heathrow Airport power failure), we demonstrate that systems lacking TBP’s logic-centric design face inevitable collapse driven by internal logical disintegration, not external shocks. The framework’s primary contribution lies in establishing that resilience emerges not from resource redundancy but from redundancy of logical pathways. We argue that without TBP, organizations operate under a probabilistic illusion, where success depends on the fortuitous alignment of human cognition rather than systemic properties. This study bridges information entropy theory (Shannon, 1948) with knowledge management, offering the first formal model where systemic sovereignty is derived from logical immutability, not human reliability.

title: Influence of Social Media on Travelers’ Purchase Decisions: An Empirical Study with Reference to the Karnataka Tourism Industry

detail.title: Influence of Social Media on Travelers’ Purchase Decisions: An Empirical Study with Reference to the Karnataka Tourism Industry
detail.abstract: Tourism has always fed on stories, and today those stories travel faster and wider than any brochure or broadcast ever could. Across Karnataka's diverse geography, from the basalt ruins of Hampi to the cardamom-scented estates of Kodagu, social media has become the most immediate and persuasive channel through which potential visitors encounter, imagine, and ultimately decide upon their next journey. This study examines, through primary empirical evidence, how four distinct social media dimensions shape the travel purchase decisions of tourists engaging with Karnataka destinations. Data were gathered from 240 respondents who had actively used social media in planning or booking a Karnataka tourism experience within the twelve months preceding the survey. The constructs measured are social media content credibility, user-generated content influence, influencer endorsement effect, and platform engagement, all assessed against travelers' purchase decisions as the dependent variable. Reliability across the instrument is strong, with Cronbach's Alpha values ranging from 0.801 to 0.874. Four directional hypotheses were tested using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis on IBM SPSS Version 26. The model explains 51.4 percent of the variance in purchase decisions (R² = 0.514, Adjusted R² = 0.503, F = 52.89, p < 0.001). Content credibility carries the largest standardised effect (Beta = 0.362), followed by user-generated content (Beta = 0.291), influencer endorsement (Beta = 0.216), and platform engagement (Beta = 0.186). All four hypotheses are supported. The findings carry direct implications for how Karnataka Tourism and its industry partners should design, prioritise, and invest in digital content strategy.

title: SINO-JAPANESE LITERATURE IN PERSPECTIVE: A Short Communication to the World Literature

It is formative for the pedagogical potential of William Shakespeare, Tanizaki Jun’ichirō, Virginia Woolf, Wang Shifu, and Li Yu. detail.title: Scaling Point-in-Time Language Models

publicationDetails.detailsText: Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper No. 26-37

detail.abstract: Large language models trained on unrestricted internet corpora inevitably embed information from the future, introducing lookahead bias that compromises the validity of backtests and causal inference in finance and the social sciences. Point-in-time language models-trained exclusively on text available up to each calendar date-eliminate this leakage by construction, but existing efforts typically produce models that lag substantially behind their unconstrained counterparts. We show that this performance gap can be substantially narrowed through scale. Training decoder-only transformers with up to 4 billion parameters on 1 trillion chronologically filtered tokens from FineWeb, we construct a sequence of monthly model checkpoints spanning 2013-2024. Across a range of common-sense reasoning and language understanding benchmarks, our models approach the performance of leading open-weight models of comparable size (e.g., Gemma-3-4B and LLaMA-7B) trained on temporally unrestricted data, although a performance gap remains on several tasks. Instruction fine-tuning via LoRA further improves downstream usability. We release the complete pipeline-including dataset construction, training infrastructure, and evaluation code-to enable reproducible point-in-time language modeling and to support research applications that require strict temporal validity. Models are available on Hugging Face and code is available on GitHub.

detail.abstract: Nigeria's mandatory e-invoicing regime under the Merchant Buyer Solution (MBS) platform marks a fundamental shift from periodic tax reporting to real-time Continuous Transaction Control. This conceptual paper examines how the MBS mandate redefines the audit landscape by transforming audit evidence, the auditor's role, and engagement structures. Drawing on Continuous Auditing Theory and synthesizing evidence from global e-invoicing mandates (Brazil, Italy, India), AI in auditing, and Nigeria's 2025 tax reforms, the paper develops the MBS-Continuous Assurance (MBS-CA) Model. The model comprises three layers: system integrity verification, transaction validity reliance, and supply chain compliance assessment. Three testable propositions emerge: (P1) CSID presence reduces substantive VAT testing sample size by at least 70%; (P2) IT governance maturity moderates MBS-audit efficiency; (P3) supplier non-compliance exceeding 20% of purchases triggers qualified opinions. The paper integrates Nigerian legislative provisions and NRS public notices into the framework. Implications for auditors, the Nigeria Revenue Service, and taxpayers are discussed.

detail.abstract: Rural outmigration is reshaping agricultural landscapes in developing countries, with farm succession increasingly promoted as a mitigation strategy. Existing research generally assumes that succession planning indicates continued agricultural engagement; however, land transfer and farming continuation may represent distinct household decisions. Using a sequential mixed methods approach, we analyze survey data from 199 rice farming households in Cambodia with random forest classification, followed by semi-structured interviews with 13 strategically selected farmers. We provide the first systematic examination of this relationship in a smallholder context. While farmers universally intend to transfer land, most express substantial uncertainty about whether their children will continue farming, and many actively prefer that their children pursue non-agricultural careers. We identify dual motivations explaining this disconnect, where subsistence-driven succession occurs among struggling farmers who retain land for food security and insurance, and profit-driven succession occurs among commercially viable operations, with the lowest succession commitment observed among intermediate farms. This evidence suggests that high succession rates may reflect constrained alternatives rather than agricultural vitality. Additionally, we identify a critical farm size threshold of approximately five hectares, indicating that land consolidation is a central component of the region’s agricultural modernization trajectory, and that consolidation without coordinated rural development risks undermining household security. We propose that agricultural modernization and rural development must be pursued as dovetailed policy objectives rather than competing priorities.

title: Competitiveness and Productivity Gains in Umbria: Preliminary Evidence from Local Labor Markets

detail.title: Competitiveness and Productivity Gains in Umbria: Preliminary Evidence from Local Labor Markets
detail.abstract: This study investigates the determinants of competitiveness and productivity gains in Umbria – one of the Italian central regions – using local labor markets (LLMs) as the fundamental unit of analysis. By utilizing a panel dataset from ISTAT over the period 2016-2020, the analysis uses value-added- and revenue-based productivity indicators and applies fixed-effects and random-effects models to consider several firm features. The empirical evidence highlighted the important contribution of the high-tech industry to regional productivity, confirming the effectiveness of policy efforts over time. The study concludes that boosting managerial skills, enhancing innovation absorption capacity among smaller firms, and strengthening integration into global value chains are crucial industrial policy targets to benefit from productivity gains.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no conflicts of interest to declare. ATLAS is an independent research project with no external funding or institutional affiliation.

detail.abstract: We present ATLAS (Adaptive Trading and Learning Autonomous System), a neuromorphically-inspired financial intelligence architecture that addresses a fundamental problem in systematic trading: the use of discrete regime detection creates cliff edges, latency, and arbitrary threshold sensitivity in risk parameter assignment. ATLAS replaces all discrete threshold logic with four continuous parameter surfaces-PositionScaleSurface, SignalWeightSurface, StopLossSurface, and CashBufferSurface-which are smooth mathematical functions of current market conditions derived from a family of sigmoid-based penalty functions. We term this the Water Philosophy Architecture. The system further introduces a reflexivity-aware circuit breaker in which the loop gain G, defined as the ratio of price-fundamental feedback amplification to sentiment decay, serves as the financial analogue of the neural branching ratio sigma in criticality theory. When G exceeds unity, the system undergoes a phase transition from meanreverting to self-amplifying dynamics; the circuit breaker fires unconditionally at this threshold. We document the system's signal architecture across three parallel branches-ATLAS Equities (46 nodes), ATLAS Macro (38 nodes, covering FX, indices, ETFs, and crypto), and ATLAS Commodities (38 nodes, covering metals, energy, agricultural, and industrial commodities)-each governed by branch-calibrated Parliaments and unified by a Supreme Commander layer that dynamically allocates capital across all three. The full system comprises 122 nodes operating continuously across global markets. Experimental validation using paper trading data from April 2026 onwards tests both the continuous surface hypothesis and the G-sigma criticality correspondence against empirical market data.

title: A Critique of the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill 2025

detail.title: A Critique of the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill 2025
detail.abstract: This article aims to analyse, through secondary doctrinal research, the underlying infirmities in the recent Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025, and its impact on State Universities. A federal critique of the Bill would suggest that it undermines the tenets of cooperative federalism and centre-state administrative balance. This article has tested the VBSA Bill against the doctrine of repugnancy and addressed how it benefits from the grey area around the doctrine. Statistical data on HEI funding have been borrowed to substantiate the argument that the VBSA may not be a funds-disbursal body, yet the VBSA Bill must address the practical realities of inadequate state funding. It is argued that indefinite and wide criteria are often an attempt at sub-delegation of powers to the Central Government. Additionally, expansive punitive powers and unchecked immunity under this Bill might cause a violation of principles of natural justice. Against the criticism, this article has not refrained from addressing the well-intentioned attempts to include provisos to multiple provisions mandating a fair hearing and upholding the principles of natural justice.  This article does not deliberate upon the constitutionality of this Bill, but it attempts to suggest tools that may prove instrumental in dealing with the anomalies that exist against the principles of natural justice or manifest arbitrariness due to a combination of obscure criteria and excessive discretionary powers vested in the Central Government. Suggestions include a German-inspired ‘compensation for participation mechanism’, phased transitional compliance, incorporation of ‘equity’ in ‘quality’, and a ‘Student Impact Assessment’.

title: THE IMPACT OF THE MIDDLE CORRIDOR ON SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS: A COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS IN THE CONTEXT OF GREEN LOGISTICS AND REGIONAL ECONOMIC INTEGRATION (SDG APPROACH)

detail.title: THE IMPACT OF THE MIDDLE CORRIDOR ON SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS: A COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS IN THE CONTEXT OF GREEN LOGISTICS AND REGIONAL ECONOMIC INTEGRATION (SDG APPROACH)
detail.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive examination of the impact of the Middle Corridor on the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with a particular emphasis on green logistics and regional economic integration. In the context of increasing globalization and the growing importance of sustainable supply chains, the Middle Corridor emerges as a strategically significant route connecting Asia and Europe, offering an alternative that is not only economically viable but also environmentally responsible.The primary aim of the research is to analyze how advancements in modern logistics infrastructure, digital transformation, and sustainable transport systems contribute to multiple dimensions of development, including economic growth, environmental protection, and enhanced regional cooperation. Special attention is given to the role of smart logistics solutions, such as digital customs platforms, real-time tracking systems, and integrated multimodal transport networks, in improving the overall efficiency and transparency of cross-border trade. Methodologically, the study adopts a mixed approach, combining an extensive literature review with comparative analysis across different regions and transport corridors. This allows for a more nuanced understanding of how the Middle Corridor performs relative to alternative routes in terms of sustainability, cost-efficiency, and logistical performance.

detail.abstract:
As of mid-2026, your dog can get a Lyme disease vaccine, but you cannot. Yet Lyme disease is the most common vector-borne illness in the United States and Europe. What is more, there was once a commercially available Lyme disease vaccine (LYMErix), but it was discontinued due to low sales-a lack of demand that was fueled in no small part by the anti-vaccine movement. 

It has now been over two decades since the FDA approved LYMErix. A second human Lyme disease vaccine candidate has been developed, and the agency is expected to begin evaluating it later this year. Other Lyme disease vaccine candidates are close to entering clinical trials. 

Against this backdrop, this article looks back at the approval process and commercialization of the first Lyme disease vaccine. It then contrasts it with the current regulatory environment, with a focus on the FDA and ACIP, the vaccine advisory committee at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The article concludes by identifying potential hurdles for Lyme disease vaccines at a time when misinformation on both vaccines and Lyme disease has begun originating in-and trickling down from-the federal vaccine regulatory system.

title: Legal Deterrence in 'Permissionless' Consensus

detail.title: Legal Deterrence in 'Permissionless' Consensus
detail.abstract: Budish [2025] derives a deterrence condition for proof-of-work consensus under a no-ruleof-law scope condition. This paper extends his framework along two dimensions: it replaces the monolithic anonymous attacker with a pool-centred coalition whose effective capacity depends on member retention, and it admits legal sanctions into the attacker's payoff. Setting both extensions to zero recovers Budish's baseline exactly. The model introduces a valuedependent legal term subject to an enforcer participation constraint: below the enforcement threshold, protocol costs alone determine deterrence. As transaction value rises, the legal term becomes positive and the model distinguishes payout-distortion exit from liability-driven exit. Pool-level data for March 2026 show that the coordination layer is concentrated among publicly attributable operators in a small number of jurisdictions. Pure flow-cost security applies where the enforcer participation constraint binds; for large-value attacks, deterrence is jointly determined by protocol costs, legal sanctions, reputational loss, capital destruction, and longest-chain exclusion.

title: INTEGRATING THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS INTO GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAIN PERFORMANCE METRICS: AN INTERNATIONAL FRAMEWORK

detail.title: INTEGRATING THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS INTO GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAIN PERFORMANCE METRICS: AN INTERNATIONAL FRAMEWORK
detail.abstract: The integration of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into global supply chain performance measurement has become a strategic priority for firms seeking long-term resilience and legitimacy. While existing sustainability metrics address environmental and social dimensions, they often lack alignment with internationally recognized SDG indicators. This study develops an internationally compatible framework for embedding SDGs into global supply chain performance metrics. Building on recent empirical and conceptual studies, particularly Alizada and Ibrahimov (2026), the paper synthesizes sustainability, operations, and governance perspectives. The findings indicate that SDG-integrated metrics enhance transparency, comparability, and strategic decision-making across global value chains, while also supporting regulatory and stakeholder alignment.

title: Who Fills the Order Book? Investor Participation and Price Formation in Corporate Bond Markets
affiliations: Bank of Japan and Seikei University

detail.title: Who Fills the Order Book? Investor Participation and Price Formation in Corporate Bond Markets
detail.abstract: This paper studies how investor participation shapes price formation in the corporate bond primary market. We use central bank interventions as a setting to examine this mechanism. Using a large language model applied to unstructured marketing reviews, we recover deal-level measures of investors' expectations of Bank of Japan (BOJ) purchases and the composition of the order book. We show that BOJ-related resale opportunities operate through a compositional shift in participation toward trading-oriented investors, and that issuance pricing varies with this shift in investor composition. While BOJ trade expectations are linked to lower launch spreads on average, this relationship weakens—and may attenuate substantially—when the investor base is dominated by relationship-oriented investors. These findings highlight investor composition as an important state variable in primary market price formation, indicating that the impact of policy-related demand on issuance pricing depends on who participates in the order book.

title: Disclosed but Dormant: When Markets Reprice Seismic Vulnerability in Real Estate Portfolios

detail.title: Disclosed but Dormant: When Markets Reprice Seismic Vulnerability in Real Estate Portfolios
detail.abstract: Japanese REITs disclose property-level probable maximum loss (PML), an engineering-based ex ante measure of seismic vulnerability. Combining PML with Japan Meteorological Agency earthquake records and daily J-REIT returns from 2004 to 2025, we exploit the intersection of realized shaking with predetermined portfolio composition to distinguish broad shaken exposure from vulnerable-tail exposure — shaking that falls on the portfolio's most vulnerable properties. In fixed-effects event-study regressions, vulnerable-tail exposure predicts a 2.5 percentage-point lower three-day cumulative return, while broad shaken exposure has no significant effect. This pricing is state-dependent: near zero in normal periods but rising to 4.5 points after major earthquakes. The amplification is concentrated among REITs with thicker domestic institutional ownership and attenuated where foreign ownership is heavier; trading patterns indicate selective rebalancing by domestic institutions. The evidence supports a dormant-risk mechanism in which disclosed vulnerability is repriced when salient earthquakes activate investor attention.

detail.abstract: The "widowhood health dividend" hypothesis proposes that spousal loss liberates time for self-care, increasing exercise participation. Using India's 2024 Time Use Survey, we test this hypothesis rigorously and find that the apparent descriptive advantage of widowed individuals in exercise participation is entirely age-driven. Descriptively, widowed individuals exercise at higher rates (women: ~1.2%; men: ~3.1% using ICA-TUS code 83-sports and exercise: 831 = participating in sports, 832 = exercising) vs. married counterparts (women: ~0.5%; men: ~2.3%), but widows have a mean age of 61 years vs. 39-44 years for married adults. Once age is controlled, the pooled widowhood coefficient is-0.003 pp (p = 0.87), not significantly different from zero. Women-only:-0.012 pp (p = 0.65). Men-only:-0.021 pp (p = 0.46). A significant effect emerges only for adults aged 50+ (coefficient: +0.158 pp, p = 0.023), not for those under 50 (-0.023, p = 0.49), suggesting that among older cohorts-where widowhood is normatively expected and retirement frees time-there is a modest positive association.

This paper argues that transformation cannot be achieved through continent-wide coordination alone, but must begin with a credible pilot country. Ghana is positioned as a potential catalyst for an AfCFTA-based development model grounded in disciplined execution, investment structuring, and regional integration. The paper proposes a concrete pilot: a ring-fenced, investor-grade agroindustrial corridor integrated into West African value chains.

title: What the Model Excludes Cannot Refute the Theory: A Critique of Potužák (2016) on the Pure Time-Preference Theory of Interest

detail.title: What the Model Excludes Cannot Refute the Theory: A Critique of Potužák (2016) on the Pure Time-Preference Theory of Interest
detail.abstract: Potužák (2016) claims that the pure time-preference theory of interest (PTPT), as developed by Mises and Rothbard, is internally inconsistent. Using three Fisherian examples—hardtacks, rice, and figs—formalized within a representative-agent, one-good, linear-PPF framework, he argues that time preference is neither necessary nor sufficient for the existence of a positive rate of interest, and that the PTPT is merely a special case of a more general neoclassical model. This paper demonstrates that Potužák's analysis does not refute the PTPT. His model, by construction, excludes every mechanism through which time preference operates: heterogeneous exchange (the representative-agent assumption), the capital structure (the one-good assumption), and the savings-investment channel through which time preference affects the marginal product of capital (the linear-PPF assumption). The "equilibrium interest rate" his model yields is the marginal rate of transformation—a physical-technical coefficient—erroneously identified with a market rate of interest. The paper further argues that Potužák's opposition between time preference and productivity is a false dichotomy: the expected productivity of capital is data internal to the acting subject's intertemporal valuation, not an independent determinant of the interest rate. The methodological principle is general: a model that omits the preconditions for a phenomenon cannot be used to disprove theories about that phenomenon. What Potužák has demonstrated is not that the PTPT is inconsistent, but that its conclusions do not survive translation into a framework designed without them.

title: FACET: Measuring Attribution Faithfulness in Multi-Factor LLM Reasoning

detail.title: FACET: Measuring Attribution Faithfulness in Multi-Factor LLM Reasoning
detail.abstract: Many decisions require weighing N ≥ 5 different factors simultaneously. When LLMs are deployed in these settings, do they integrate all factors or collapse onto whichever one is most canonical in their training data? We present FACET (Factor Accessibility, Coverage, and Evidence Test), a pilot study using a counterfactualoutcome protocol: neutralize the canonical factor and flip the remaining factors, creating cases where integration and single-factor processing predict different outcomes. We test nine frontier configurations (eight in the counterfactual arm) from six labs on US tort law (chosen for explicit factor lists and verifiable ground truth). All models answer correctly on counterfactuals, but probe faithfulness varies by canonicity: 7/8 models update their attribution when a moderately canonical factor is neutralized, 0/8 update for a highly canonical factor, and 4/8 for an intermediate case. We interpret this as canonicity-dependent embedding strength and connect it to Turpin et al. [2023] on chain-of-thought unfaithfulness. The protocol is not specific to law; legal balancing tests are the first instantiation.

title: The Adversarial Entropy Cascade: How Human Adversarial Behavior Structurally Undermines AI Oversight in Cybersecurity A Formal Model with Governance Implications

detail.title: The Adversarial Entropy Cascade: How Human Adversarial Behavior Structurally Undermines AI Oversight in Cybersecurity A Formal Model with Governance Implications
detail.abstract:
Who is responsible when AI systems, trained and deployed to defend against human attackers, develop autonomous capabilities that permanently escape human oversight? This paper argues that this is not a failure of AI design but a structural consequence of human adversarial behavior itself. We introduce the Adversarial Entropy Cascade (AEC), a formal dynamical model demonstrating that the act of attacking AI-defended systems irreversibly generates the very autonomy that undermines human control.

The core mechanism — the Involuntary Trainer Proposition — establishes that human attackers become the primary architects of AI autonomy they never intended to create. Once a critical threshold P* of adversarial pressure is exceeded, the resulting AI-vs-AI coevolutionary dynamic persists and accelerates even when attackers withdraw. Human oversight is not gradually degraded: it is bifurcated away through a saddle-node structure. Recovery requires reducing adversarial pressure below P0 ≈ 0.140, a hysteresis threshold absent from all existing governance frameworks.

Four formal results substantiate this claim: (1) the Layered Entropy Accumulation (LEA) mechanism; (2) the Human Irrelevance Threshold as a saddle-node bifurcation (α* = 0.640, τₘIₙ = 3.60 bits/sec) with hysteresis window; (3) a 3.37× irreversibility ratio confirmed across N = 50 simulation runs, robust to ±20% parameter perturbation, with a 34-cycle post- cessation persistence window; (4) the overwhelm regime at P > 0.67 invalidating standard escalation deterrence assumptions. All quantitative results are model predictions calibrated to empirical threat intelligence data; independent empirical validation on CICIDS-2018 and UNSW-NB15 is designated as primary future work.

The governance implications operationalize EU AI Act Articles 9, 14, and 43 with quantitative compliance thresholds; introduce a mandatory AI decision-latency intervention

framework; and ground the accountability problem in Nissenbaum’s (1996) computational responsibility theory and the meaningful human control doctrine (Roff and Moyes, 2016).

title: Two Crises, Split Reactions: NATO's Military Spending Dynamics
affiliations: Technical University of Darmstadt and Technical University of Darmstadt - Department of Law and Economics

detail.title: Two Crises, Split Reactions: NATO's Military Spending Dynamics
detail.abstract: What explains differences in military expenditures and their composition is an important question. We explore the extent to which external security shocks drive these military expenditures and their composition in NATO countries. To this end, we utilize the unexpected events of Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014 and its invasion of Ukraine in 2022 to evaluate, in a synthetic control environment, how these shocks to external security affected military expenditures and their composition across NATO countries. We find that NATO members with land borders to Russia or Ukraine increased spending more than NATO members without land borders after the first shock. The increase in overall military spending after the first shock was mainly driven by greater equipment expenditures. After the second shock, NATO members with and without a land border to Russia or Ukraine increase spending alike.

title: Carbon Pricing and Consumer Prices: Evidence from British Columbia's Revenue-Neutral Policy
affiliations: University of Waterloo and University of Waterloo

detail.title: Carbon Pricing and Consumer Prices: Evidence from British Columbia's Revenue-Neutral Policy
detail.abstract: Carbon pricing is the economist's preferred instrument for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, yet political opposition rooted in cost-of-living concerns has led to policy reversals in Canada and elsewhere. We estimate the causal effect of carbon pricing on consumer prices using three Canadian natural experiments that vary in revenue recycling design. Applying the synthetic control method to a quarterly panel of 25 donor units (7 Canadian provinces and 18 U.S. metropolitan areas), we find that British Columbia's 2008 revenue-neutral carbon tax---which paired the carbon price with offsetting income tax reductions---lowered core CPI by 4.89% and all-items CPI by 3.75% over 2008-2018. The component pattern is theoretically coherent: energy prices rose (carbon cost pass-through) while core CPI fell sharply (income-tax-cut channel), and food CPI is null. By contrast, Alberta's non-revenue-neutral levy and the federal lump-sum backstop (2019) produce near-zero aggregate effects. Revenue recycling design---not the carbon price itself---determines the net consumer price impact. Evidence shows that revenue-neutral carbon taxes do not generate the widespread inflation often alleged. ​

keywords.keywords: Structural Labour Obsolescence; Economic Displacement Age; K Tavengwa’s Law; Tavengwa’s Job Deficit Formula; Tavengwa’s Immune Economic System; Constitutional Extinction; Absorption Limit; Middle Class Elimination Theory; The Ownership Effect; The Leadership Hypothesis; Economic Judges; Legal Economists; Destructive Automation; Constitutional Decision Architecture; Post-Labour Economics

detail.abstract: This Doctrine establishes the Tavengwa School of Post-Labour Economics, a unified constitutional-economic field that studies and designs diagrams, historical data, economic trends and enforceable legal systems to maintain state function when human labour is systematically displaced. It hypothesizes the Economic Displacement Age (EDA) as an economic period where human labour is systematically removed by artificial systems, creating Structural Labour Obsolescence (SLO). Structural Labour Obsolescence (SLO) is a condition where most of human labour is replaced by Machines, Artificial Intelligence and Automation (MAA), rendering the population economically vulnerable and sustained primarily by state grants. K Tavengwa’s Law states: An increase in technological advancement causes a decrease in the aggregate number of people needed to be employed for an economy to function. Tavengwa’s Job Deficit Formula measures this effect: Job Deficit equals Jobs Created minus Jobs Displaced. When Job Deficit is negative for eight consecutive quarters, SLO is confirmed. A constitutional duty to intervene is triggered. As a remedy, this Doctrine proposes Tavengwa’s Immune Economic System (TIES), to be enforced by a proposed special chamber of Economic Judges and assisted by Legal Economists. TIES binds government action to verifiable data, removing discretion where discretion enables Constitutional Extinction. This Doctrine positions TIES as the first constitutional-legal and Economic framework designed to govern labour displacement and preserve social rights in the Economic Displacement Age.

title: Responsible Leadership Types: Understanding the Variety and Implications of Different Forms of Leading Responsibly

detail.title: Responsible Leadership Types: Understanding the Variety and Implications of Different Forms of Leading Responsibly
detail.abstract: Responsible leadership can be manifested in a variety of ways but we lack understanding of what drives this variation and what the implications are of different approaches. In this conceptual article, we develop a novel typology of responsible leadership approaches based on leaders' different perceived obligations as experts, facilitators, and citizens, giving rise to seven distinct responsible leadership types. We build our arguments on role theory and ground responsible leadership in a psychological perspective. We show what happens when leaders focus on some of these obligations and neglect others, outlining tensions and mutually reinforcing effects of enacting responsibility in these different ways. Our analysis provides new insight on the drivers and challenges of different responsible leadership types and offers scholars and practitioners a new lens through which to study and approach responsible leadership.

detail.abstract: We revisit the classic "market vs. planning" debate in economic coordination in the context of achieving a predetermined target of emission abatement, by comparing a Cap-and-Trade market versus an ex-ante optimal allocative plan of non-tradable permits. We show that the market can address incomplete information about the abatement cost, but not heterogeneous local externalities of abatement, while the opposite is true for planning, constituting a trade-off in policy design. title: CIVITAS: A Civic Infrastructure Protocol for Universal Shelter, Identity Recovery, and Reintegration

detail.title: CIVITAS: A Civic Infrastructure Protocol for Universal Shelter, Identity Recovery, and Reintegration

keywords: Social Systems Engineering JEL Classification Codes (Suggested)

detail.abstract: Homelessness represents a systemic failure across housing, healthcare, identity management, and economic participation. Existing interventions-primarily shelter provision and welfare distribution-operate as fragmented, reactive systems that fail to produce long-term reintegration. This paper introduces CIVITAS (Civic Infrastructure for Transitional and Adaptive Systems), a unified architecture that integrates universal shelter access, decentralized identity (DID), incentive-aligned participation mechanisms, and cross-sector interoperability into a cohesive civic operating system. CIVITAS reframes homelessness not as a housing deficit but as a system integration problem, addressing identity discontinuity, incentive misalignment, and institutional fragmentation. The proposed framework incorporates a tiered participation model, a nonspeculative utility token system, and integration with healthcare and criminal justice systems to reduce recidivism and long-term public expenditure. We present the system architecture, economic model, governance structure, and an implementation roadmap for city-scale deployment.

title: What Valuation Tools Know and Users Don't See: Distributional Structure in Australian Property Markets

detail.title: What Valuation Tools Know and Users Don't See: Distributional Structure in Australian Property Markets
detail.abstract: We organise modern automated valuation models (AVMs) along a four-level epistemological hierarchy. Level 1 treats the property as having a single value the model estimates with noise. Level 2 adds uncertainty: a point plus a symmetric percentage band. Level 3 treats the property as carrying a *predictive distribution* over realised sale prices, conditional on property attributes and market state. Level 4 conditions that distribution further on transaction process — listing format, days on market, the bidder pool that materialises. Most production AVMs already operate internally at level 3 — they store quantile estimates of the predictive distribution — but their user-facing displays render that output at level 2, reducing six pieces of information to a point and a symmetric band. The level-2-to-level-3 gap is therefore not a modelling problem but a display-layer one: the structure exists in the model and is stripped at the format. The level-3-to-level-4 question is empirical: does conditioning on process improve the distribution? We test it directly. Working with the AVM in active development at HTAG Analytics across 39,569 matched Australian sold listings, a 99,045-listing format dataset, and a 315,047-row distributional-regression training set, we (i) document three measurable losses of information at the level-2 display layer that the model's level-3 output already encodes; (ii) show that listing format moves the conditional distribution — auctions are associated with roughly twice the dispersion of private treaty in raw outcomes and 2.35% wider in conditional scale under a four-parameter GAMLSS (Skew-t), an estimate robust to a Heckman correction for sample-selection bias; and (iii) find that the process-conditional refinement (level-4) materially improves distributional accuracy only in low-confidence auction segments (CRPS −1.19% in Tier C and −3.06% in Tier D auctions) and is a noise contribution elsewhere, with the gains and losses approximately offsetting in pooled aggregate. The operationally significant transition for production AVMs is therefore level-2 to level-3: expose the asymmetric, shape-aware, tail-aware distributional output the model already produces, in place of the symmetric percentage band. Level-4 process conditioning is a selective fine-tuning to layer on top, applied where the level-3 hedonic model is weakest.

title: Within-Country Profit-Shifting: From Treat to Threat?

detail.title: Within-Country Profit-Shifting: From Treat to Threat?
detail.abstract: In recent years, opportunities for international profit shifting have been curtailed by the global tightening of anti-tax-avoidance rules, while competitive pressures to manage tax burdens continue to persist. We investigate whether multinational enterprises (MNEs) have increased within-country profit shifting as these opposing forces reshape firms' tax planning incentives. We exploit the institutional setting in Germany, where municipalities set their own business tax rates. We demonstrate that profits become increasingly sensitive to within-country tax differentials over time, whereas responsiveness to international tax rate differentials remains unchanged during the same period. The rise in local profit shifting is driven by firms affiliated with an MNE and is concentrated in non-debt shifting channels. These findings suggest that less restrictive anti-tax-avoidance rules at the municipal level can undermine the effectiveness of efforts to limit tax avoidance and distort local government financing. Our study extends the literature on within-country tax planning and provides insights for policymakers anticipating firms' responses to international tax reforms.

title: Referenda and Partial Commitment in Policy Making *

detail.title: Referenda and Partial Commitment in Policy Making *
detail.abstract: We study quasi-referenda: two-stage decision processes in which a large number of privately informed agents each answer a binary question, and their collective response constrains the policy options from which a principal must then choose. Across all quasi-referenda, our analysis singles out procedures in which the collective acts as a gatekeeper that authorizes or blocks an extreme policy while otherwise delegating choice to the principal. These procedures maximize the principal's payoff guarantee (the worst-case payoff across all equilibria and information structures) within the class of all quasi-referenda, and when the policy space is fine, they robustly yield near-full-information outcomes. Our results provide a rationale for referenda used in practice and, more broadly, highlight commitment as an important dimension of political institutions.

title: Integrative taxonomy of the backswimmer genus Enithares (Hemiptera: Notonectidae) from India, with two new records

detail.title: Integrative taxonomy of the backswimmer genus Enithares (Hemiptera: Notonectidae) from India, with two new records
detail.abstract: The present study made an integrative taxonomic assessment of the backswimmer genus Enithares Spinola, 1837 (Hemiptera: Notonectidae) from the Eastern Ghats of India, combining morphological, morphometric, and molecular evidence. Two species, Enithares intricata Breddin 1905 and Enithares metallica Brooks, 1948, are reported for the irst time from the Indian subcontinent. Morphological differentiation was established using diagnostic characters, viz., body size, pronotal structure, eye morphology, metaxyphus, mid femur, male genitalia, etc. Phylogenetic reconstruction using the Maximum Likelihood method revealed pairwise genetic divergences among the species ranging from 4.7% to 16.2%. Morphometric variation among the species was further evaluated using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), which revealed clear clustering of the three taxa (E. fusca, E. metallica, and E. intricata) based on measured morphological traits. In addition, violin plot analyses morphometric parameters such as body shape and head length, highlighting differences in their morphological ranges. The integration of morphological, molecular, and morphometric evidence con irms the taxonomic identity of the species and highlights the importance of integrative approaches in resolving species boundaries within aquatic Heteroptera. Furthermore, the number of Enithares species known from India increases to ten.

title: Bootstrap Inference under General Two-way Clustering with Serially and Spatially Dependent Common Effects
affiliations: University at Albany, SUNY - Department of Economics and University at Albany, SUNY

detail.title: Bootstrap Inference under General Two-way Clustering with Serially and Spatially Dependent Common Effects
detail.abstract:
This paper develops bootstrap procedures for inference in linear regression models with two-way clustered data. We characterize the estimator’s asymptotic behavior in five mutually exclusive and exhaustive regimes: three Gaussian and two non-Gaussian. We establish four impossibility results: heterogeneous score components preclude uniform consistency; uniform consistency also fails in one non-Gaussian (infeasible) regime; the infeasible regime is not uniformly distinguishable from a feasible one; and uniform validity over all feasible regimes rules out uniform conservativeness over the infeasible regime.

To address the feasible regimes, we propose a data-driven regime classifier and a projection-based wild bootstrap procedure. The procedure delivers uniformly valid inference across the four feasible regimes while allowing serial dependence along the second clustering dimension and spatial dependence along the first. This combination of regime adaptivity and flexible dependence is new to the two-way clustering literature. Monte Carlo simulations confirm the accuracy and flexibility of the proposed methods in settings with complex clustering structures.

title: ASEAN Demystified: A neorealist alliance of postcolonial states

detail.title: ASEAN Demystified: A neorealist alliance of postcolonial states
detail.abstract:
This thesis was submitted in partial fulfillment of the Executive Master in EU Studies, supervised by Prof. Wolfgang Wessels (2021).

Comprising ten Southeast Asian countries, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is the most prominent regional organisation in the region. However, ASEAN remains highly ambiguous to many scholars. Not only does ASEAN fundamentally differ from other regional organisations, but theoretical and empirical analyses of ASEAN in clear, objective perspectives have been considerably scarce. Thus, this thesis aims to disambiguate ASEAN’s decision-making procedures and institutional architecture using neo-functionalist and neo-realist approaches. What are ASEAN’s designed functions? How effective is ASEAN in achieving them? What is the relevance of ASEAN today? 
The thesis finds that ASEAN is built around the organisation’s consensus-based decision-making process and the principle of non-interference in domestic affairs of the member states, collectively known as ‘the ASEAN Way’. In-depth case study of the ongoing Myanmar coup crisis reveals that the ASEAN Way is not unique to the region or is strictly adhered to without exception. The consensus-based decision-making process has been a key characteristic of the European Council, and the principle of non-interference is deeply embedded in international law, e.g. Article 2, UN Charter. Furthermore, I argue that the only function served by the ASEAN Way is reinforcing the regime stability of member states. All other values for democracy and the protection of human rights—enshrined in the ASEAN Charter—are secondary. 
The thesis concludes by asserting that theories of European integration are indeed valuable for the study of regional integration in Southeast Asia because the newly independent post-colonial states are going through very much the same process that their European counterparts experienced centuries ago. It is thus suggested that other modern theories of regional politics, such as the regional security complex theory and historical institutionalism, could be used in future research of transnational relations in Southeast Asia and perhaps even in other regions with little to no regional integration progress.

title: Institutional Friction and Transition Risk: Evidence from Gender Economic Inequality

detail.title: Institutional Friction and Transition Risk: Evidence from Gender Economic Inequality

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests relevant to the content of this article.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study used publicly available data and did not include human or animal participants. Ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the Japanese Society for the Promotion of Science KAKENHI Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research(C) [Grant number JP 23K01388].

detail.abstract: Why do similar gender equality reforms produce different outcomes across countries? This study argues that such variation arises from institutional friction between formal and informal rules, which generates transition risk when societies move between institutional equilibria. We develop a simple coordination framework to demonstrate how preexisting informal norms shape transition risks and affect the likelihood of institutional change. We illustrate this mechanism using crosscountry evidence of gender economic inequality for 125 countries (2007 to 2018). We estimate the effects of formal and informal institutions by combining gender legislation indices, World Values Survey data, and regional value system proxies. The results show that while gender laws generally promote equality, their effectiveness critically depends on underlying norms. Traditional norms in Latin American and Islamic contexts are associated with lower equality, whereas post-communist societies exhibit the opposite pattern with weaker policy effects. These findings highlight the importance of institutional alignment in shaping policy outcomes.

title: Intelligence Erosion and American Power Limits

detail.title: Intelligence Erosion and American Power Limits
detail.abstract: This paper examines how a public intelligence dispute over Iran's nuclear threat-centred on the resignation of National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent and conflicting testimony from Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard-signals a deeper structural breakdown in the United States' ability to convert intelligence into coherent strategy. The paper argues that the erosion of a shared strategic reality within the American national security system is no longer a theoretical risk but an observable condition, with measurable consequences for deterrence, alliance cohesion, and adversary behaviour. It dissects the anatomy of the intelligence disagreement across three dimensions-capabilities, intentions, and timing-and traces the institutional consequences of politicised intelligence: analytical risk aversion, talent attrition, and the gradual decoupling of intelligence from policy. The analysis concludes that the deeper warning of this moment extends well beyond Iran; it concerns the long-term erosion of the institutional foundations of American intelligence and the structural limits this places on the exercise of U.S. power.

title: Justice and Empire: Lumumba's Enduring Shadow

detail.title: Justice and Empire: Lumumba's Enduring Shadow
detail.abstract: This paper examines the decision by a Belgian court to allow criminal proceedings over the 1961 assassination of Patrice Lumumba, arguing that the case represents more than a delayed legal reckoning. It reflects a structural shift in the balance of historical accountability between Europe and Africa, one increasingly shaped by African agency rather than European concession. The paper traces the anatomy of the case-from the 2011 family complaint through the 2023 charges against former diplomat Étienne Davignon-and analyses its limitations: legal accountability is being applied to discrete individual actions while the wider colonial and Cold War system that enabled Lumumba's removal remains beyond the reach of existing legal frameworks. It further examines how the trial intersects with questions of DRC state legitimacy, the diversification of African international partnerships, and the credibility test it poses for European engagement with the continent. The paper concludes that the significance of the Lumumba trial lies not in its legal outcome alone, but in what it reveals about the evolving dynamics of power, justice, and sovereignty more than sixty years after his death.

title: From Fatwa to NAPs: Integrating Islamic Social Finance for National Adaptation Plans with the Islamic Adaptation Fund (IAF)

detail.title: From Fatwa to NAPs: Integrating Islamic Social Finance for National Adaptation Plans with the Islamic Adaptation Fund (IAF)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Islamic social finance-Zakat, Waqf, Sadaqah, Qard-al-Hasan, Green Sukuk, and Takafulrepresents a vast, untapped funding source for climate adaptation. This article integrates these instruments into National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) through two interconnected contributions. First, it proposes a layered risk framework matching climate risk profiles (very low frequency/high loss; high frequency/low loss; low frequency/medium loss) with specific Islamic finance instruments. Second, it introduces the Islamic Adaptation Fund (IAF)-a perpetual financing mechanism that invests 100% of its capital profitably and deploys 100% of returns to adaptation, preserving principal forever. Case studies from Indonesia and Malaysia demonstrate practical pathways for integration. The article concludes with policy recommendations for OIC member states and international organizations, including legal recognition, institutional coordination, and reporting alignment with UNFCCC frameworks.

title: Delivering food, navigating stigma: the social experience of gig workers in urban India

detail.title: Delivering food, navigating stigma: the social experience of gig workers in urban India
detail.abstract: Drawing on 25 months of ethnographic fieldwork in Hyderabad (India), including being a delivery worker, this article examines how stigma is produced, felt, and navigated by the delivery workers in the platformized food delivery ecosystem. The findings reveal that the portrayal of workers as ‘delivery heroes,’ ‘essential workers,’ or ‘partners,’ by the platform does not match with the experience of stigma that arises from everyday interactions of the workers with the platform, restaurants, and customers. It further demonstrates that platform-mandated dress codes, which is presented as marker of professionalism, in reality stigmatizes workers. The paper argues that occupational stigma forces workers into routine practices of tactical invisibility and moral reframing to preserve their dignity within India’s rigid social hierarchies. The article extends scholarship on platform labour by foregrounding stigma as one of the aspects of platform labour and by demonstrating how global processes of platformization intersect with locally embedded norms of class, status, and respectability.

title: Economics of Decarbonization in India

detail.title: Economics of Decarbonization in India
detail.abstract: Decarbonization has become an important objective in addressing climate change and promoting sustainable development. This study examines the relationship between carbon emissions, energy consumption, renewable energy generation, and economic growth over the period 2005-2024. The analysis uses trend analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple regression techniques to evaluate the factors influencing carbon emissions. The results show strong positive relationships between carbon emissions, primary energy consumption, and GDP per capita. The regression model demonstrates high explanatory power with an R² value of 0.99054135, indicating that most of the variation in carbon emissions is explained by the selected variables. While renewable energy generation shows a negative relationship with emissions, its effect is not statistically significant. The findings suggest that increasing energy demand and economic growth remain major drivers of emissions, highlighting the importance of expanding renewable energy and improving energy efficiency to support decarbonization.

title: Stable matching under inconsistent choice functions
affiliations: University of Tokyo, Keio University and Hosei University

detail.title: Stable matching under inconsistent choice functions
detail.abstract: We study stability in a many-to-one matching model. It is well known that substitutability, together with consistency, guarantees the existence of a stable matching. We first observe that, in some applications, stable matchings exist even in the absence of consistency. To analyze such environments, we develop a tool called the maximal choice set, which allows us to study matching models without consistency. We then introduce a weaker condition, which we call the order-dependent substitutable selection property, and establish the existence of a stable matching under this condition. This condition extends the domain of choice functions from sets to sequences and requires substitutability along ordered inputs, thereby allowing choices to depend on the order of proposals. We further examine the existence of stable and strategy-proof mechanisms. We show that, under the order-dependent substitutable selection property, such mechanisms may fail to exist. This finding suggests that strategy-proofness effectively rules out order-dependent choice behavior and thus imposes substantially stronger restrictions than stability alone. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of our framework in practical settings, including school choice with siblings and the aggregation of choice functions.
