title: Arthashastra to Modern Banking : Ancient Indian Financial Wisdom in Comtemporary Practice

detail.title: Arthashastra to Modern Banking : Ancient Indian Financial Wisdom in Comtemporary Practice

declarations.funderStatement: Neha Chawla

detail.abstract: The study titled "Arthashastra to Modern Banking: Ancient Indian Financial Wisdom in Contemporary Practice" explores how the economic and financial principles of Kautilya's Arthashastra remain relevant in today's banking system. The paper provides an overview of ancient Indian financial practices, including lending, interest regulation, treasury management, taxation, risk assessment, and ethical wealth handling, and compares them with modern banking methods to show their continuing significance. A review of existing literature highlights previous research on ancient Indian economics, financial systems, and their connections with contemporary banking practices, emphasizing the value of integrating traditional knowledge with modern financial strategies. The methodology includes qualitative analysis of the Arthashastra text and comparative study with modern banking policies and practices. Findings reveal that principles such as ethical lending, strategic financial planning, and risk mitigation from the Arthashastra closely align with current banking operations, demonstrating their practical relevance. The study concludes that ancient Indian knowledge systems offer meaningful insights for building ethical, efficient, and sustainable financial practices in the modern world. Key references include Kautilya's Arthashastra, research papers on ancient Indian finance, and modern banking studies.

title: Political Violence and the Rise of Fascism *
affiliations: Catholic University of Milan,  and University of Bologna - Department of Economics

detail.title: Political Violence and the Rise of Fascism *
detail.abstract: In the early 1920s, the Italian fascist movement grew from a marginal group into an organized party capable of challenging incumbent political forces and precipitating democratic backsliding. A key driver of this expansion was the strategic use of violence by coordinated squads that moved across municipalities to intimidate opponents and undermine democratic institutions. We show that road networks were central to the diffusion of fascist violence: by lowering travel times and facilitating rapid incursions, roads made violence both harder to anticipate and more effective at the local level. We document that such violence profoundly altered local political institutions, destabilizing existing arrangements and accelerating the consolidation of fascist control within a few years.

title: An Instability Criterion for Galerkin FEM Solvers of the Fokker-Planck Equation with SUPG Stabilization

detail.title: An Instability Criterion for Galerkin FEM Solvers of the Fokker-Planck Equation with SUPG Stabilization
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Financial Péclet Number Pe_h = b·h/(2D), a dimensionless criterion governing whether a Galerkin FEM solver of the Fokker–Planck equation produces spurious oscillations. The main theorem proves that the Oscillation Index satisfies OI = max(1, Pe_h) for even element counts, with a closely related formula for odd counts. SUPG stabilization with the Franca–Frey parameter achieves nodal exactness (OI = 1) for the one-dimensional CD problem via exponential fitting. For the Vasicek CDR problem, the reaction term amplifies Galerkin oscillations to OI = 104 at the resonance mesh (n = 14, Pe_h = 1.06); this is approximately 98× the CD lower bound, while SUPG stays below unity (mild over-diffusion rather than oscillation). Rolling 63-day estimates from three major equity markets (S&P 500, DAX 40, Nikkei 225) confirm that |Pe_h| exceeds unity in 82–87% of calendar windows at a conventional mesh, making instability the empirical default. A Federal Funds Rate backtest quantifies regulatory capital misallocation at a median of €2.4M per €100M book (95th percentile €16.4M) across 1,422 unstable windows; at the same resonance mesh the relative VaR error can reach 213%, though this is a peak-mesh figure, not the typical magnitude. The paper provides a mesh selection criterion, a block-bootstrap significance test, and a conjectured extension to the two-dimensional Heston model.

title: Predictors of Climate Change Concern and Climate Policy Support: An Analysis Across Asian Economies
affiliations: Independent, Asian Development Bank, Asian Development Bank, Asian Development Bank and Asian Development Bank

detail.title: Predictors of Climate Change Concern and Climate Policy Support: An Analysis Across Asian Economies

publicationDetails.detailsText: ADB Economics Working Paper Series No. 843

detail.abstract: Public support for climate policies that improve the region's resilience is crucial given climate risks. This paper contains the analysis of data from 13,547 respondents across 14 Asian economies, following a survey completed in July 2024. The analysis reveals widespread climate concern (91% of respondents see it as a serious problem), with notable differences across economies (28%–81%). Support for climate policies varies. Low carbon infrastructure receives broad backing (50%–76%) while support for carbon taxation is mixed (37%–74%). Respondents aged 55 and above generally demonstrate stronger policy support than younger ones. Income effects reveal an inverted U-shaped relationship, with middle-income households (those earning $25,000– $49,999 annually) showing the highest support. Econometric analysis identifies policy awareness as the variable most strongly associated with support, followed by personal climate experiences and demographic factors. Opposition stems from concerns over economic burden, implementation effectiveness, and fairness. While climate concern varies across economies, policy support is more uniform, suggesting adaptable policy design principles. These findings suggest the need for targeted communication and policy designed to address economic impacts and implementation concerns.

title: Generative AI and Algorithmic Academic Coloniality in Higher Education: Implications for English Language Teaching

detail.title: Generative AI and Algorithmic Academic Coloniality in Higher Education: Implications for English Language Teaching
detail.abstract: The rapid uptake of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education is reshaping practices of writing, knowledge production, and language use. While Literature examined both the coloniality of English Language Teaching (ELT) and the ethics of AI, limited attention has been paid to their intersection. This conceptual paper argues that generative AI should be understood not simply as a norm-setting infrastructure, but as a continuation and intensification of academic coloniality within ELT. Situating AI within a longer trajectory of linguistic imperialism, the paper proposes the concept of 'algorithmic academic coloniality' to capture how AI systems standardise language, filter epistemic diversity, and reinforce 'Global North' knowledge systems. As AI becomes embedded in academic practice, it mediates what counts as legitimate expression while rendering its regulatory power less visible. The paper outlines implications for pedagogy, linguistic diversity, and knowledge production in higher education.

detail.abstract: In a lab-in-the-field experiment with experts facing risky, higher-stakes decisions, experts exhibit context-dependent reversals in their attitudes toward risk, and these reversals are affected by the likelihood of a better outcome, i.e., the direction of preference reversals is affected by the proximity of a better outcome to certainty. Although these patterns cannot be explained by leading models from economics and psychology, they can be explained by a model that combines stochastic reference dependence from economics and context-dependent sensitivity from psychology. The interaction of these two mechanisms may explain the perplexing inconsistencies in people's choices, including those attributed to probability weighting.

title: Choice under Value Pluralism

detail.title: Choice under Value Pluralism
detail.abstract: Classical rational choice theory assumes preferences are complete, presupposing that an agent's evaluative considerations have a common scale. We drop completeness and develop a normative theory of rational choice for agents whose values are plural and incommensurable. The resulting individual choice problem is characterized as the formal dual of Arrovian social choice. The agent's value structure determines a majority tournament whose cycle topology partitions choice behavior into three classes: classical optimization, recovered when values converge; the hard choice, in which value conflicts are structurally isolated; and the tragic choice, in which conflicts are entangled and all classical consistency properties fail. Violations of classical consistency conditions are rational responses to value conflict rather than departures from rationality.

title: Barriers to Reentry: Initial Borrowing Frictions, Refinancing, and Wealth Redistribution

detail.title: Barriers to Reentry: Initial Borrowing Frictions, Refinancing, and Wealth Redistribution

detail.abstract: This paper examines how frictions encountered during the initial home purchase mortgage origination process shape borrowers' future refinancing behavior and long-term financial outcomes. Leveraging variation in loan officer workload as a quasi-random source of origination delays, I find that experiencing a 60+ day delay reduces quarterly refinancing rates by 16-24%. Exposure to these origination frictions is disproportionately concentrated among minority borrowers, low-income households, and those with lower credit scores, with evidence consistent with lender bias contributing to racial disparities. I quantify the cost of origination delays using both a back-of-the-envelope calculation and a model-based simulation, which imply present-value overpayments of approximately $6,500 to $8,500 per delayed borrower. I also evaluate policy alternatives including streamlined refinancing, automatic refinancing, and type-specific pricing, using the simulations to show how each option affects refinancing behavior and total mortgage payments.

title: Downwind of the Bus Lane: Transit Pollution and Academic Performance
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Wisconsin-Madison

detail.title: Downwind of the Bus Lane: Transit Pollution and Academic Performance
detail.abstract: We estimate the effect of air pollution from Bogotá's Bus Rapid Transit system on high school test scores. Using wind direction interacted with bus route intensity as an instrument, we find that schools more frequently downwind of BRT corridors score significantly lower in math and global exams. The instrumental variable estimates imply that an additional μg/m3 of PM2.5 reduces math scores by 0.10 standard deviations and global scores by 0.09 standard deviations, with no effect on language. NOx and PM10 show similar negative effects. Girls and students from higher-income households experience larger declines. A georeferenced household survey provides suggestive evidence that respiratory disease mediates the pollution-achievement relationship. These results reveal a human capital cost of diesel-powered transit and underscore the importance of cleaner fuel technologies in urban transportation policy.

title: Generation, Verification, and the Direction of R&D
affiliations: and Anhui University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Generation, Verification, and the Direction of R&D
detail.abstract: Knowledge production combines generation and verification-two stages that use different resources and scale at different speeds. The decomposition creates a within-R&D allocation problem that one-step knowledge production models cannot represent. Because non-directed R&D subsidies scale up aggregate research effort without changing its internal composition, they cannot correct this allocation-a structural insufficiency that follows from the new object's existence. Industries where verification relies on unpriced public resources face the largest AI-driven productivity losses; industries with fully priced verification are unaffected-a ranking testable without point estimates.

title: The International Law Fallacy: A Forensic Analysis of Selective Enforcement in Maritime Risk Systems and Sovereign Risk Environments

detail.title: The International Law Fallacy: A Forensic Analysis of Selective Enforcement in Maritime Risk Systems and Sovereign Risk Environments

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents a structured analytical examination of divergence between formal legal obligations and observable institutional behavior within contemporary international governance systems. It introduces the concept of Statutory Inactivity, the retention of authority without corresponding execution, defined as the condition in which institutions retain clear legal authority yet fail to apply enforcement uniformly across materially comparable situations.

Using a comparative case framework, the analysis contrasts the rapid international response to maritime risk conditions in the Strait of Hormuz with the absence of equivalent intervention in large-scale water diversion affecting host cities of the 2026 World Cup in Mexico. These events are evaluated as parallel instances of operational exposure occurring under conditions of demonstrable jurisdiction, authority, and risk visibility.

The paper further develops the Soltani Order, an analytical framework identifying recurring patterns of enforcement divergence, asymmetrical exposure allocation, and structural coherence maintained alongside selective activation of authority. A quantitative risk amplification model is introduced to demonstrate how strategic conditions translate legal unpredictability into measurable financial exposure.

This work establishes a documented reference point for evaluating the relationship between legal structure and operational reality in the early twenty-first century, establishing a structured basis for evaluating institutional behavior under conditions of geopolitical and regulatory variability.

title: Audit-safe decision-aware conformal forecasting for storage arbitrage in electricity markets
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Audit-safe decision-aware conformal forecasting for storage arbitrage in electricity markets
detail.abstract: Highlights Decision-aware conformal bounds support battery arbitrage decisions. Anytime-valid e-processes audit deployed lower bounds. Stress-aware gating improves profits versus scalar conformal gating. Realistic tests include degradation and inter-day state of charge. Abstract Electricity storage operators require price uncertainty that can be translated into dispatch decisionsand monitored after deployment. This paper develops an audit-safe decision-aware conformalforecasting framework for battery arbitrage. The method combines an hour-specialized stackedprice forecaster with conformal lower bounds on operational value, post-selection correction,stress-aware recalibration, and an anytime-valid reliability audit. We evaluate the frameworkin two linked public benchmarks: a three-market daily-cycle benchmark used to identify thecontribution of each component, and a seven-market realistic battery benchmark with degradation,round-trip efficiency, receding-horizon dispatch, and inter-day state-of-charge carry-over. Theresults show that decision-level conformalization improves the simplified benchmark whilereducing loss-day frequency, and that the stress-aware schedule gate delivers positive gainsover the best scalar conformal gate in all seven realistic markets, with no audit alarm crossing.Relative to an unconstrained point-dispatch baseline, the conformal gates sacrifice some averageprofit but substantially reduce downside exposure and provide continuously auditable reliability.The evidence supports a bounded applied conclusion: conformal prediction is more useful forelectricity-market operation when it is deployed as a decision-control and audit layer rather thanas a standalone interval report.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly participates in economic interactions not only as a tool, but also as an autonomous bargaining counterpart negotiating on behalf of firms, platforms, and consumers. Yet little is known about how humans respond psychologically and strategically when bargaining with such agents in dynamic settings. We study this question in a laboratory experiment using a three-stage alternating-offer bargaining game in which participants negotiate in real time with either another human or a GPT-based AI agent. We also introduce a human-beneficiary condition in which the AI agent's earnings may affect another participant's payment. Agreements are not reached earlier in human-human bargaining than in human-AI bargaining, but they are reached significantly earlier when the AI's payoff has human consequences. Human proposers offer more to human opponents than to AI agents, whereas responders become significantly more willing to accept unfair AI offers when AI earnings may benefit another human. These findings suggest that fairness and reciprocity toward AI are weaker and more conditional than toward humans, but partially re-emerge when AI outcomes affect real people. The results have implications for the design of AI negotiation systems and broader human-AI economic interactions.

title: Does Green Factory Certification Improve Corporate Credit Financing? Evidence from Voluntary Environmental Programs
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Does Green Factory Certification Improve Corporate Credit Financing? Evidence from Voluntary Environmental Programs
detail.abstract: Voluntary Environment Programs (VEPs) become a critical approach to aligning environment protection with corporate economic development. However, how particularly debt providers, internalize the signals conveyed by VEPs remains largely underexplored. This paper examines the impact of Green Factory Certification on corporate credit financing. Using Chinese A-share listed companies from 2010-2024 as sample, and employing staggered difference-in-difference model, we show that green factory certification significantly reduces financing cost and increases long-term debt proportions. title: Green Financial Policies and Renewable Energy Investment: Evidence of Policy Interactions with Energy Taxes in OECD Countries
affiliations: Northeastern University, Northeastern University at Qinhuangdao and Harbin Institute of Technology

detail.title: Green Financial Policies and Renewable Energy Investment: Evidence of Policy Interactions with Energy Taxes in OECD Countries
detail.abstract: Green finance policies have emerged as pivotal instruments for renewable energy investment efforts amid global climate change. However, the interaction between green finance policies and traditional regulations, such as energy taxes, has been insufficiently explored in existing research. To address this gap, this study uses panel data from 30 OECD countries (2000-2020) to analyze the combined effects of green finance and energy taxes through panel regression and moderation models. The analysis provides four key insights. First, green finance policies significantly promote renewable energy investment, a finding confirmed by extensive robustness checks. Second, energy taxes negatively moderate this relationship. A higher energy tax burden attenuates the positive impact of green finance policies, indicating potential policy conflicts. Third, the effectiveness of green finance policies exhibits contextual heterogeneity. The impact is stronger in economies in the catching-up phase and those with energy-intensive industrial sectors. Fourth, while energy taxes show synergy with green finance in countries receiving lower development assistance, conflicting effects arise in economies with high energy consumption in the tertiary sector. Consequently, policymakers should implement differentiated policy portfolios based on national development stages. Green finance policies and energy taxation must be dynamically coordinated to mitigate conflict and enhance investment efficiency, thereby accelerating the energy transition.

title: Quantifying the Labor Potential of Older Adults in China: Untapped Potential or Overwork? Evidence from CHARLS Panel Data

detail.title: Quantifying the Labor Potential of Older Adults in China: Untapped Potential or Overwork? Evidence from CHARLS Panel Data
detail.abstract: Accurately assessing the residual work capacity of China's older population is central to delayed retirement reform design, yet most empirical estimates rely on cross-sectional data that cannot control for unobserved individual heterogeneity or adequately capture the structural divide between urban and rural labor markets. This study re-evaluates the latent labor supply of adults aged 55–79 using five waves of panel data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011–2020). Applying the Cutler–Meara–Richards-Shubik (CMR) counterfactual framework alongside individual fixed-effects models, we construct health-based predictions of labor force participation and compare them with observed rates. Panel attrition tests confirm the longitudinal representativeness of the sample. The results reveal a striking asymmetry across demographic groups. Urban men aged 60–69 face a persistent participation shortfall relative to their health-predicted capacity—a gap that widened from 20.75 percentage points in 2013 to 26.08 percentage points in 2018—pointing to binding mandatory retirement constraints. Rural populations and women in specific age cohorts, by contrast, exhibit participation rates that routinely exceed health-based predictions, a pattern consistent with health-adjusted overwork driven by limited pension coverage and economic necessity.These findings suggest that older adults in China do not constitute a uniform reserve of labor supply. Instead, untapped work capacity and health-discordant overwork coexist across different institutional and demographic groups, implying that policy discussions on later-life employment should pay closer attention to structural heterogeneity.

detail.abstract: Indonesia hosts the world's largest Muslim population and has positioned the sharia economy as a national development agenda, yet the way mainstream economic media represents this agenda has not been systematically mapped. We present a text clustering analysis of one year of Indonesian online economic news on the sharia economy. From 1,429 articles published by CNBC Indonesia between January 2025 and January 2026 containing the keyword syariah, a context-conditioned relevancy classifier [Apriandito et al., 2026a] retains 230 articles judged as economically relevant; TF-IDF vectorization, K-Means clustering, and silhouette analysis then partition this subset into a topical map. The analysis identifies fourteen clusters that organize into six thematic groupings: sharia banking, sharia capital markets, the halal real economy, sharia gold, macro-monetary policy, and fiscal policy. Three discourse patterns emerge. First, sharia frequently appears as a side mention rather than the subject of the article: half of the clusters are dominated by general macro or fiscal vocabulary, with sharia surfacing as a tag rather than as a topic. Second, when sharia is the subject, financial topics dominate while only one cluster addresses the halal real economy. Third, Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) appears as a recurring institutional reference across four of the fourteen clusters. Together, these patterns describe a nested structure in which sharia is often peripheral, sharia coverage is mostly financial, and sharia financial coverage is centered on a single institution. The paper contributes an empirical baseline for the structure of Indonesian sharia economic discourse and a method that other studies of Indonesian thematic discourse can adapt.

title: The Role of Upfront Investment Subsidies and Energy Prices for Heat Pump Adoption - Evidence from Germany
affiliations: University of Leipzig and University of Leipzig

detail.title: The Role of Upfront Investment Subsidies and Energy Prices for Heat Pump Adoption - Evidence from Germany
detail.abstract: This paper examines how changes in upfront investment subsidies and energy prices are associated with heat pump adoption, and analyzes how the effectiveness of these incentives depends on heat pump technology and building characteristics. Using a panel of all 401 German counties from 2012 to 2019, we analyze four market segments: air-source (ASHP) and ground-source heat pumps (GSHP) in existing and new buildings. We estimate correlated random-effects Poisson models with Mundlak means to separate within-county from between-county variation. We find that upfront investment subsidies are strongly associated with ASHP adoption, especially in existing buildings, and less with GSHP uptake. Higher electricity-to-gas price ratios are associated with lower heat pump adoption across counties, whereas within-county estimates suggest little to no association. The association is stronger for GSHP than for ASHP adoption, and within each technology it is weaker in new than in existing buildings. Based on our estimates, back-of-the-envelope calculations suggest that, for ASHPs, upfront investment subsidies are more cost-effective per ton of CO$_2$ avoided than energy-price subsidies, whereas for GSHPs the ranking is likely reversed. We also find heating degree days to be negatively associated with ASHP adoption and positively associated with GSHP adoption.

title: India's Asymmetric Path to AI Diffusion

detail.title: India's Asymmetric Path to AI Diffusion
detail.abstract: Public-market discourse on India's role in the global artificial-intelligence economy has concentrated almost entirely on the lower layers of the AI stack-energy generation, data-centre infrastructure, and capital expenditure commitments by domestic conglomerates exceeding USD 225 billion. We argue this framing is incomplete, and probably mispriced. Adapting the five-layer stack proposed by Huang (2026), we develop the Application Layer Hypothesis: that India's structural comparative advantage in AI diffusion lies not in compute, models, or chips, but in the application of AI to the country's exceptionally large stock of operationally inefficient mid-market services businesses. We model this mechanism through the transition from Software-as-a-Service to Service-as-a-Software (Vardhan & Mukherjee, 2026), and decompose the resulting output gain via the identity Output = Capacity × Utilisation × Yield. Using a representative Indian specialty-clinic chain as a case, we show how AI deployment can drive a 35× enterprise-value uplift through three compounding channels: margin expansion, addressable-pool expansion at zero marginal cost, and multiple re-rating from services to healthcare-infrastructure. We further argue that India's diffusion path is structurally distinct from Western (private-led, legacy-bound), East Asian (state-coordinated, hardware-centric), and Chinese (state-platform) trajectories: India follows a public-rails / private-app hybrid characterised by long lags followed by non-linear diffusion at inflection-a pattern observed in mobile telephony, payments, and digital identity. We estimate the cumulative GDP unlock of this transformation in the order of USD 50 trillion over a 25-year compounded horizon, concentrated in domestic consumer services serving the unmonetised next billion. Implications for capital allocation, public policy, and the literature on technological leapfrogging are discussed.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a monetary framework that combines the discipline of hard-money systems with a bounded, rule-based liquidity mechanism. The model eliminates fractional reserve banking by separating fully backed deposits from credit creation and introduces a pre-funded liquidity buffer that can be activated during periods of financial stress. Unlike fiat systems, which rely on discretionary and potentially unlimited monetary expansion, the proposed framework maintains a fixed monetary base while allowing limited internal adjustment through reallocation of reserves. The objective is not to eliminate economic cycles, but to reduce systemic instability arising from the interaction between money creation and credit expansion. The framework draws on existing ideas from full-reserve banking, narrow banking, and hard-money traditions, while introducing a capped liquidity mechanism within a fixed-supply system. This proposal is presented as a conceptual model intended to stimulate further research rather than a fully specified policy design.

title: Market-Based Campaign Finance Reform
affiliations: University of Arizona - Department of Economics and Loeb & Loeb

detail.title: Market-Based Campaign Finance Reform
detail.abstract: Since the U.S. Supreme Court's 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission, so-called "Super PACs" have spent heavily in elections, raising concerns about electoral fairness and political representation. This paper evaluates a novel market-based response: Super PAC insurance. By indemnifying candidates against Super PAC expenditures, such contracts can deter outside spending and provide investor returns without public funding or legal reform. We estimate actuarially sound premiums based on a battery of models predicting Super PAC behavior. Our analysis shows that Super PAC insurance can be both financially viable and potentially effective at mitigating the influence of Super PACs.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the relationship between territorial economic concentration and the spatial distribution of high-value human capital in Bulgaria between 2021 and 2026.

It demonstrates that the country’s structural economic patterns—regional GDP concentration, human capital distribution, and sectoral productivity—remain stable even when electoral outcomes become unusually homogeneous.

The analysis introduces the concept of electoral opacity, defined as a reduction in the analytical association between structural economic conditions and observable electoral outcomes.

The paper separates explicitly:
(1) the structural layer (economic geography and human capital),
(2) the continuity layer (institutional and administrative capacity),
(3) the electoral layer (observed political outcomes).

The findings suggest that under conditions of weakened continuity, electoral outcomes may lose their informational value as indicators of underlying economic structure.

The paper is diagnostic and descriptive, providing a conceptual framework for interpreting territorial economic structures under conditions of weakened policy continuity.

title: Credit Expands, but Why Does It Become Fragile?

detail.title: Credit Expands, but Why Does It Become Fragile?
detail.abstract: Credit crises are widely understood as cascade phenomena, yet credit expansions are often modeled as linear and smooth processes. This paper identifies one mechanism through which credit expansion itself can unfold as a cascade-like process. More fundamentally, the analysis shows how systemic fragility can emerge endogenously as credit expansion reshapes economic and financial linkages by extending leverage toward marginal firms-those operating close to profitability thresholds. As a result, firms that are largely innocuous in normal times can become central to nonlinear amplification of credit contraction.

title: The Keystone Shield: An Integrated Defensive Architecture for State Cannabis Sovereignty under Federal Schedule I

detail.title: The Keystone Shield: An Integrated Defensive Architecture for State Cannabis Sovereignty under Federal Schedule I
detail.abstract: This paper presents an integrated defensive architecture for state-level cannabis programs operating under continued federal Schedule I status (or Schedule III status with regulatory vacuum). The architecture is built on three pillars. First, a pre-positioned legal defense package: an Attorney General opinion template affirming Tenth Amendment protections under Printz v. United States, New York v. United States, and Murphy v. NCAA; an interstate commerce compact template for multi-state mutual defense; and pre-drafted briefing materials for state employees facing federal inquiry. Second, a financial safe-harbor alignment strategy that reframes state banking participation from "creating a banking system" (federally exposed) to "verifying compliance with federal guidance" (aligned with the 2014 FinCEN Cole Memo framework), implemented through a closed-loop Pennsylvania payment system. Third, a federal enforcement response protocol including IRS 280E mitigation through state tax credits offsetting excess federal tax burden, executive protection orders for state employees, and a "constitutional consistency lock" tying any federal cannabis-banking retaliation to Second Amendment Preservation Act jurisprudence. The paper develops each pillar with specific statutory language, administrative procedure, and enforcement-response decision trees. The architecture is intended to convert the Anti-Commandeering Doctrine from theoretical scholarship into ready-to-deploy state policy infrastructure.

title: Germany's Gamble to Make Europe Defensible

detail.title: Germany's Gamble to Make Europe Defensible
detail.abstract: Germany's 2026 military strategy—its first standalone defense document since the Second World War—marks a fundamental redefinition of the Bundeswehr's institutional role within NATO and European collective defense. Rather than pursuing classical great-power military status through force-size expansion, Berlin is repositioning itself as the indispensable framework power of European conventional deterrence: the state whose geographic centrality, logistical infrastructure, and reserve depth make alliance warfighting operationally coherent rather than merely declaratory. This paper examines the strategy's core conceptual shift from inventory-driven to effects-oriented force planning, its introduction of a 'one-theater doctrine' integrating NATO, Middle Eastern, and Indo-Pacific security dynamics, and its elevation of reserve forces as a primary instrument of homeland defense and theater-level resilience. It further assesses the constraints—personnel shortfalls, procurement bottlenecks, administrative inertia, and political durability—that will determine whether declared institutional ambition translates into operational reality. The analysis finds that Germany's strategic vision is coherent and structurally grounded, but that its credibility ultimately rests on measurable capability milestones across readiness, procurement, infrastructure hardening, and alliance integration by the end of the decade.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a state-deviation framework to examine the consumption-income relationship in the presence of structural heterogeneity. Rather than proposing a new econometric model, the analysis identifies common income and consumption states as structural reference levels that organize cross-sectional variation in consumption behavior. The framework shows how heterogeneous intercepts and marginal propensities to consume can be systematically related through these states, allowing consumption to be expressed as deviations from a common structural benchmark. A central implication is that residual dependence between income and consumption may arise from unabsorbed structural heterogeneity. This provides a structural interpretation of endogeneity that complements conventional econometric views based on statistical misspecification. The framework also yields testable implications linking baseline consumption to income levels across economies. An empirical illustration using panel data for East Asian economies supports the proposed structure. The results indicate a systematic relationship between income and adjusted baseline consumption, consistent with the presence of structural imbalance between income and consumption states. The findings suggest that accounting for common structural states offers a coherent way to interpret crosscountry differences in consumption behavior.

detail.title: Global Coordination under Monotone Sampling *
detail.abstract: We study coordination in multi-population environments where agents revise actions after observing finite independent samples of others' behavior and applying deterministic monotone decision rules. The framework covers a broad class of commonly studied learning dynamics, and it allows heterogeneity across populations. Except for the knife-edge case in which every population simply copies one sampled action, coordination is globally stable: almost every trajectory converges to a coordinated state in which everyone chooses the same action. The proof connects monotone sampling rules to reliability functions of coherent systems. We show that relaxing independence, monotonicity, or within-population homogeneity can generate stable miscoordination.

title: A Novel Risk Forecasting Method by Fusing Deep Learning and Random Fores

detail.title: A Novel Risk Forecasting Method by Fusing Deep Learning and Random Fores
detail.abstract: A novel method is proposed for risk forecasting by integrating deep learning and random forest, which combines the respective advantages of global and local fitting. To overcome the limitations of traditional quantile regression in capturing nonlinear relationships and the drawbacks of single machine learning models, this method innovatively embeds the local similarity weights generated by quantile random forest (QRF) into the quantile loss function. Such a design encourages similar predicted values for similar samples, preserves the strength of long short-term memory (LSTM) networks in modeling temporal dependence, and improves the sensitivity to nonlinear features and extreme risks. The proposed method is tested using simulated data generated from AR and GARCH models. It achieves significantly lower mean squared error (MSE) than LSTM and QRF over the quantile range of 0.01 to 0.10, particularly in heteroscedastic data. For empirical evaluation, experiments are carried out on the S&P 500 (2018-2024) and the Shanghai Stock Exchange Composite Index (SSEC, 2017-2025). The fusion method yields the optimal prediction accuracy at most quantiles, improving risk forecasting precision by 43.73% and 65.16% over LSTM and QRF for the SSEC, and by 76.80% and 78.96% for the S&P 500, with exceptional performance at extreme quantiles. This work provides a new tool for financial tail risk quantification and a useful reference for the fusion application of machine learning models.

title: Transforming Master Data into Strategic Infrastructure: Governance Maturity, Intelligent Automation, and Enterprise Integration Leadership

detail.title: Transforming Master Data into Strategic Infrastructure: Governance Maturity, Intelligent Automation, and Enterprise Integration Leadership
detail.abstract: Master data management has traditionally been positioned as a governance discipline focused on control, standardization, and regulatory compliance. However, contemporary enterprise environments characterized by distributed cloud platforms, intelligent automation capabilities, and real time digital ecosystems demand a more strategic interpretation. This paper reconceptualizes master data as foundational infrastructure rather than administrative oversight, arguing that governance maturity, intelligent automation, and enterprise integration leadership must converge to enable sustained enterprise intelligence. Drawing upon cross-industry architectural patterns, organizational design principles, and system integration models, the study presents a structured transformation pathway that elevates master data from operational stewardship to strategic enterprise asset. The analysis explores governance capability progression, automation embedded within data lifecycle processes, and leadership frameworks required to orchestrate complex multi system environments. It further proposes an integrated maturity model linking policy enforcement, data quality intelligence, interoperability architecture, and executive accountability into a unified infrastructure perspective. By synthesizing architectural modernization, intelligent monitoring mechanisms, and cross functional stewardship alignment, the paper demonstrates how master data can support resilience, regulatory adaptability, predictive analytics, and scalable enterprise integration. The contribution advances a forward looking paradigm in which master data infrastructure functions as the connective core of intelligent enterprises, enabling value creation beyond compliance toward innovation, agility, and long term strategic advantage.

title: A Risk-Based Approach to Infrastructure Delivery under U.S. Buy America Policies

detail.title: A Risk-Based Approach to Infrastructure Delivery under U.S. Buy America Policies
detail.abstract: The Buy America framework-spanning the Buy American Act, sector-specific statutes, and the Build America, Buy America Act of 2021-advances legitimate national interests in domestic industry and supply chain resilience. Its implementation, however, imposes compounding, cross-phase compliance risk on infrastructure projects without the contractual architecture to manage it. This paper argues that the framework's structural failures-fragmented risk allocation, misaligned incentives across multi-party delivery ecosystems, and rigid contract forms ill-suited to regulatory uncertainty-are the underappreciated drivers of cost overruns and schedule delays in U.S. public infrastructure. Drawing on the JFK International Airport redevelopment as a case study, it proposes a three-pronged reform: provisional sum mechanisms to assign compliance risk to the party best positioned to manage it; performancelinked incentives to realign contractor and agency behavior; and pre-bid procurement flexibility to reduce adversarial dynamics. These reforms require no statutory amendment-they are available to contracting parties today as a matter of sophisticated contract design. Implementing them is a prerequisite for the United States to deliver on the infrastructure investment the legislation was designed to support.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether and how household relational investment-proxied by gift and favor expenditure (renqing spending)-affects formal credit access in China, using panel data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) with two-way community-year fixed effects and instrumental variable estimation. We document a robust positive effect of relational spending on household leverage that is specific to non-mortgage credit, concentrated among asset-poor households without formal collateral, and substantially larger in rural and western regions. Systematic mechanism analysis rules out generalized neighbor trust as the operative channel and shows the effect is significantly weaker for households with relatives in quasi-state and knowledge-intensive sectors-consistent with a social collateral interpretation in which particularistic network obligations substitute for formal collateral in bank lending. Cultural endowment and social tax explanations are rejected as alternative channels. Cross-sectional analysis using the 2010 CFPS baseline reveals that community public governance quality amplifies the marginal return to relational spending on credit access, while physical infrastructure exerts no moderating effect-indicating that formal community institutions and informal relational capital are complements in the credit signaling process rather than substitutes. Together, these findings characterize a specific financial inclusion mechanism through which asset-poor rural households access formal credit in institutionally thin environments, with direct implications for rural financial development policy.

These domains reinforced one another, producing a self-sustaining social order. The study contributes to scholarship on South Indian history by demonstrating how economic control and meaning systems jointly underpin sustainable social hierarchy.

detail.abstract: The Goods and Services Tax(GST) was celebrated by the midnight joint parliamentary session on June 30, 2017. The celebration event only took place twice before in the Indian parliament's history, the first time marking the 50th anniversary of the Quit India movement in 1992 and the second on the fifty years of Independence. This was the third time and first time that any non-historic achievement was celebrated in this manner, indicating the importance of the 101st Constitutional Amendment in the history of India. This was the goal when in March 1986 the reforms for indirect taxes were started aiming for unified tax structures which were finally achieved on July 1, 2017, initiated by the UPA government in 2009. (Express Web Desk, 2017) The policy sparked debates about its implementation, efficiency, federal relation between state and centre, and impact on India's economy. This analysis employs the Pentagon model to examine the GST Act by the Centre, focusing on policy willingness. It discusses critical lessons that can be drawn from the GST rollout to improve the effectiveness of similar large-scale reforms in the future. Through the concepts of problem identification, formulation, adoption and policy implementation, this study seeks to understand the role of policy willingness in informing future reform and offering insights to optimise large-scale policy implementation in India.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of multi-constellation low Earth orbit (LEO) systems has intensied concerns regarding congestion, coordination burden, and equitable responsibility allocation among operators. We present a scenario-driven simulation framework for comparative multi-operator governance analysis under stated assumptions, together with an AI-assisted triage module. The framework evaluates policy-relevant risk and workload proxies in a controlled simulation environment, rather than true collision probabilities or operational space situational awareness. We compare three governance regimesR0 (uncoordinated), R1 (soft coordination), and R2 (fairness-aware enforcement)across four locked multi-operator scenarios spanning growth, mixed compliance, elevated uncertainty, and exogenous shock conditions. We then export an event-level machine-learning dataset and frame unresolved coordination burden as a decisionsupport target (dataset label: unresolved_required_action). On grouped held-out evaluation (grouped by scenario and Monte Carlo seed), we compare Logistic Regression, XGBoost, and MLP models, using a dummy baseline for calibration context; XGBoost performs best on the primary grouped test split. Results remain non-operational in interpretation. In the simulation layer, coordinated regimes outperform R0 on governance-sensitive proxies, while R1 and R2 are numerically close on core safety proxies. In the AI layer, primary grouped-test discrimination and ranking metrics support prioritization, but leave-one-scenario-out (LOSO) generalization is mixed, with weaker transfer especially under held-out growth-like conditions. Taken together, the evidence supports AI-assisted risk triage as analyst-facing decision support within the simulation workow, not autonomous control or operational SSA.

title: The Centralization Paradox: Centralized Expertise and Decentralized Chaos in Business Analysis Centers of Excellence

detail.title: The Centralization Paradox: Centralized Expertise and Decentralized Chaos in Business Analysis Centers of Excellence
detail.abstract: Business analysis centers of excellence (BACoEs) promise to standardize practices, scale expertise, and drive enterprise-wide improvement, yet many produce the opposite: fragmentation, shadow capabilities, and dissolution. This study examines the mechanisms underlying this paradox through a comparative case study of 18 BACoEs, drawing on 64 semi-structured interviews, 285 documents, and 24 months of observation. Three failure patterns emerged: the Ivory Tower pattern (33%), prioritizing methodological purity over operational pragmatism; the Bottleneck pattern (28%), generating shadow capabilities averaging $2.3 million in annual redundant spending; and the Orphan pattern (11%), in which executive sponsor departure led to dissolution. Successful BACoEs maintained executive sponsorship continuity (4.8 versus 2.3 years), proactive demand management, scalable operating models, and outcome-based metrics. This study extends paradox theory by demonstrating how structural choices amplify or resolve centralization-decentralization tensions, introduces the construct of stable undesirable equilibria to explain intransigent failure cycles, and quantifies paradox costs to enable economic analysis of resolution strategies.

detail.abstract: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), launched in 2015, represents India's most ambitious affordable housing initiative, targeting "Housing for All" through two parallel streams PMAY-Urban and PMAY-Gramin. This policy review examines the scheme's legislative foundations, operational objectives, enforcement mechanisms, and real-time implementation outcomes across urban and rural India. Drawing on official dashboards, PIB data, and a district-level case study of Bhagalpur, Bihar, the paper finds that while PMAY has achieved notable scale  with over 89 lakh urban houses completed by December 2024 — significant gaps persist between sanctioned and completed units, particularly in southern states. The review identifies systemic challenges including delays in fund disbursement, beneficiary selection discrepancies, outdated exclusion criteria, and inadequate stakeholder coordination. It recommends adopting blockchain-based monitoring, viability gap funding, streamlined disbursement mechanisms, and greater participation of Gram Sabhas and Urban Local Bodies to enhance scheme efficacy and ensure the program's inclusive development goals are fully realized.

title: Evaluating a large international bank's OKR rollout using universal deployment parameters

detail.title: Evaluating a large international bank's OKR rollout using universal deployment parameters
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the rollout of the Objectives and Key Results (OKR) framework within the Personal & Business Banking (P&BB) unit of a large international bank (BANK) over the period 2022-2026. Using Ben Lamorte's universal OKR deployment parameters as an analytical reference, the study examines how OKRs were operationalized, adapted, and refined over time in a large, highly regulated financial institution. Rather than applying the deployment parameters ex ante, OKRs at BANK P&BB emerged through an iterative process of experimentation, learning, and redesign. Drawing on a longitudinal single-case study design and informed by the author's dual role as OKR Lead and researcher, the paper systematically assesses choices related to organizational level, number of OKRs, scoring methods, cycle length, alignment mechanisms, and the relationship between OKRs, KPIs, and performance management.

detail.title: Zenvy: A Blended Blockchain Framework for Clear E-Commerce and Confirmed Final-Mile Logistics
detail.abstract: This paper presents Zenvy, an e-commerce platform that uses blockchain to coordinate five different roles: Manufacturer, Supplier, Logistics, Delivery Agent, and Customer. The backend is built on Java Spring Boot and connects to a custom SHA-256 blockchain. MongoDB handles data storage, JWT handles login, and RBAC controls who can do what. A React frontend gives each role its own dashboard, and a sidebar shows the ledger updating live. Payments are held in escrow and only released once the delivery is cryptographically verified. We tested the system in three deployment setups. Blockchain verification added less than 5% latency, and consistency between nodes stayed at 99.2%. The platform handled up to 1000 users at once with block finality under 2.3 seconds. The paper contributes (1) a working multi-role blockchain framework for real supply chains, (2) role-specific dashboards with live ledger updates, (3) a smart contract escrow that releases funds through a state machine, and (4) a visualization platform for tracking, dispute resolution, and audit trails.

detail.abstract:
This article critically examines the evolving legal framework governing the use of force and the right of self-defence in international law, with particular emphasis on anticipatory self-defence and state responsibility. While Article 2(4) of the United Nations Charter establishes a general prohibition on the use of force, exceptions under Article 51 and customary international law, most notably "The Caroline doctrine", have created interpretation flexibility that is increasingly susceptible to misuse.

The paper argues that anticipatory self-defence, though not expressly codified, has gradually acquired legitimacy through state practice and judicial interpretation; however, the absence of uniform evidentiary thresholds and consistent application has enabled powerful states to expand its scope beyond the requirements of necessity and proportionality. Through an analysis of landmark cases such as Nicaragua v. United States, the Kosovo advisory proceedings, and state practices in the Arab–Israeli conflicts and post-9/11 interventions, the article demonstrates how ambiguity within the legal framework has weakened the collective security regime envisioned under the UN Charter.

Further, the article examines the attribution of non-state actors’ conduct to states through the effective control test and highlights the resulting expansion of state responsibility. It contends that while international law provides parallel mechanisms of state and individual accountability, significant enforcement gaps persist, particularly in relation to non-state actors and inconsistent Security Council responses.

The article concludes that the contemporary doctrine of self-defence requires clearer legal thresholds and more consistent institutional application to prevent its instrumentalization. Strengthening evidentiary standards, limiting discretionary interpretations, and reinforcing collective security mechanisms are essential to preserving the integrity of international law and ensuring accountability in the use of force.

detail.abstract:
Исследование посвящено разработке аналитического фреймворка — матрицы структурной классификации субъектов малого и среднего предпринимательства (МСП) — на основе двух теоретически независимых осей: типа мотивации (necessity-driven ↔ opportunity-driven) и стадии реализации предпринимательского потенциала (потенциал ↔ действие). Пересечение осей формирует четыре квадранта (Q1–Q4), каждый из которых требует дифференцированного набора инструментов государственной политики. На основе количественного анализа данных по Кыргызской Республике за 2017–2025 годы выявлен системный дефект действующей модели господдержки: субсидированное кредитование через коммерческие банки консервирует доминирование квадранта Q3 («выживание») и не стимулирует переход субъектов в Q4 («трансформация»).

This paper develops an analytical framework — the Matrix of Entrepreneurial Potential and Driven Action (MPDA) — for classifying small and medium enterprises (SMEs) along two theoretically independent axes: motivational type (necessity-driven vs. opportunity-driven) and stage of realization (potential vs. action). The intersection of these axes yields four quadrants (Q1–Q4), each requiring a distinct set of government interventions. Drawing on quantitative analysis of Kyrgyz Republic data for 2017–2025, the study identifies a structural flaw in the existing support model: subsidized lending channeled through commercial banks entrenches the dominance of Q3 ("survival entrepreneurship") while failing to catalyze transitions into Q4 ("transformative entrepreneurship")

detail.title: Spiritual Leadership: One More Leadership Style? Should We Care? Absolutely!
detail.abstract: Most leaders search for ways to improve how employees grow and perform as a team and, in turn, improve organizational performance. Advice on how to lead well-heroically and successfullyis a dime a dozen. The current context, variously defined as brittle, anxious, uncertain, nonlinear, and incomprehensible, makes people anxious and fearful, which, in turn, prevents them from flowing. Amid the chaos and unprecedented change, the need for leaders to engage with their people is greater than ever. We believe that one conceptualization of leadership formed over the last 25 years, spiritual leadership (SL), can serve as an anchor to help leaders make headway in the current context. However, SL is also a concept that is poorly understood and often rejected before its usefulness is evaluated.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming industries such as healthcare, finance, education, governance, and national security. While AI offers immense opportunities for innovation and efficiency, it also presents significant ethical, legal, and social challenges. Issues such as algorithmic bias, lack of transparency, data privacy violations, and autonomous decision-making risks demand structured oversight mechanisms. This research paper explores the concept of AI oversight and examines global policy models designed to regulate responsible AI implementation. The study analyzes existing regulatory frameworks, identifies governance gaps, and proposes a balanced policy model that promotes innovation while ensuring accountability, fairness, transparency, and human rights protection. As AI systems increasingly influence critical areas such as healthcare, finance, and governance, the development of comprehensive legal frameworks becomes paramount to ensure accountability, fairness, and transparency. This research explores the evolution of legal frameworks for AI regulations, focusing on key areas such as algorithmic accountability, data privacy, intellectual property rights, and liability for autonomous decision making Through comparative policy analysis and ethical risk assessment, the paper argues that effective AI governance requires multi-stakeholder collaboration, clear regulatory standards, and adaptive policy mechanisms capable of evolving with technological advancements. The findings contribute to the growing discourse on responsible AI development and highlight the need for comprehensive oversight structures at national and international levels.

title: Cold-Start Forecasting of New Product Life-Cycles via Conditional Diffusion Models
affiliations: Peking University - Guanghua School of Management, Guanghua School of Management, Peking University, Peking University - Guanghua School of Management, Peking University and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST)

detail.title: Cold-Start Forecasting of New Product Life-Cycles via Conditional Diffusion Models
detail.abstract: Forecasting the life-cycle trajectory of a newly launched product is important for launch planning, resource allocation, and early risk assessment. This task is especially difficult in the prelaunch and early post-launch phases, when product-specific outcome history is limited or unavailable, creating a cold-start problem. In these phases, firms must make decisions before demand patterns become reliably observable, while early signals are often sparse, noisy, and unstable. Methodology/results: We propose the Conditional Diffusion Life-cycle Forecaster (CDLF), a conditional generative framework for forecasting new-product life-cycle trajectories under cold start. CDLF combines three sources of information: static descriptors, reference trajectories from similar products, and newly arriving observations when available. Here, static descriptors refer to structured pre-launch characteristics of the product, such as category, price tier, brand or organization identity, scale, and access conditions. This structure allows the model to condition forecasts on relevant product context and to update them adaptively over time without retraining, yielding flexible multi-modal predictive distributions under extreme data scarcity. The method satisfies consistency with a horizon-uniform distributional error bound for recursive generation. Across studies on Intel microprocessor stock keeping unit (SKU) life cycles and the platform-mediated adoption of open large language model repositories, CDLF delivers more accurate point forecasts and higher-quality probabilistic forecasts than classical diffusion models, Bayesian updating approaches, and other state-of-the-art machine-learning baselines. Managerial implications: Our results show how generative forecasting can support managerial judgment in cold-start settings where conventional forecasting methods are least reliable. By producing full predictive distributions and updating them as new information arrives, CDLF helps managers assess launch-stage upside potential, downside risk, and forecast uncertainty in a timely and disciplined way. More broadly, the framework provides a foundation for decision-relevant forecasting in new product launches and other operational settings characterized by limited history and rapidly evolving information.

title: The Financial Péclet Number: Analytical VaR Error Bounds Under Galerkin FEM Instability in Fokker-Planck Models

detail.title: The Financial Péclet Number: Analytical VaR Error Bounds Under Galerkin FEM Instability in Fokker-Planck Models
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Financial Péclet number Peₕ ≡ (μ-σ²/2)•h/σ² as the exact stability criterion for Galerkin finite element method (FEM) discretisations of the Fokker-Planck equation governing Value-at-Risk (VaR) in financial risk models. When the element-level Péclet number exceeds one in absolute value, the Galerkin cumulative distribution function becomes nonmonotone and VaR is computationally undefined-not merely inaccurate. The Il'in (1969) exponential-fitting scheme eliminates this instability universally with a single element and zero additional cost; it reproduces exact nodal CDF values for all Péclet numbers, with VaR error O(h²) from piecewise-linear interpolation. Calibrated to daily data from 2000 to 2026 across six assets (SPX, TLT, BTC-USD, NVDA, GLD, EWJ), Galerkin VaR is undefined in 12.8% to 59.7% of 63-day rolling windows; among defined windows, mean discretisation errors range from 25% to 37%, with 95th percentiles reaching 63% to 88%, all exceeding the 10% illustrative materiality threshold adopted in this paper. Il'in mean errors are 15-22% with zero NaN windows. An OLS regression of VaR error on the element Péclet number yields R² = 0.60-0.68 with Newey-West HAC t-statistics of 24-39 (all p < 10-130), establishing the Financial Péclet number as a continuous quantitative predictor of Galerkin FEM discretisation error. All error percentages in this paper measure FEM discretisation error relative to the exact analytical solution of the Fokker-Planck BVP-not relative to realised losses or the true GBM quantile-consistently isolating numerical error from model error.

detail.title: Tax Policy Whiplash: Recent Tax Developments and Questions They Raise
detail.abstract: The last decade has seen seismic shifts in the U.S. tax policy landscape. We argue that developments in major tax laws—the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (2017), the Inflation Reduction Act (2022), and the One Big, Beautiful Bill Act (2025)—have reshaped the U.S. tax environment by rapidly introducing a series of competing policies that introduce, reverse, eliminate, or reshape incentives (i.e., effectively inducing tax policy whiplash). In this paper, we outline features of these recent U.S. legislative tax developments and discuss some of the key tax policy and research questions they raise. We offer a succinct summary of new tax developments in the most recent law (OBBBA) and discuss how the extensions or reversals of previous laws raise compelling economic and tax policy questions. We argue that the collective movements in tax regulation provide an environment ripe for researchers to meaningfully contribute evidence to tax policy discussions.

title: The impact of internationalization and innovation on productivity across MEDA firms

detail.title: The impact of internationalization and innovation on productivity across MEDA firms
detail.abstract: The study investigated the impact of innovation and different forms of trading on firms' productivity across six MEDA transitional economies. Utilizing granular firm-level data from the World Bank Enterprise Surveys (WBESs) covering the period 2019-2020 and estimating a Cobb-Douglas production function with the Least Squares Dummy Variables (LSDV) approach, the study analyzed how different modes of international commitment-"two-way" traders, exporters, and importers-interact with innovation. The results suggested that the effects of innovation and internationalization are not uniform, rather, they are context-dependent. This means that innovation significantly boosts productivity primarily when it is combined with export activities, and particularly in tech-industries. Firms that are "two-way" traders and innovators showed superior performance, whereas the benefits for importers are less significant. Furthermore, firm-level characteristics such as management experience, human capital, and networking are robustly significant positive predictors of productivity, while family ownership showed a negative impact. The study concludes that targeted policies that jointly promote innovation and trade, particularly export, are crucial drivers for enhancing productivity across MEDA firms.

title: On the Applicability of the Legal Model of Open Environments to Earth

detail.title: On the Applicability of the Legal Model of Open Environments to Earth
detail.abstract:
This paper examines the applicability of the legal model of open environments to Earth. In prior studies, this model was developed through the analysis of spaces characterized by the absence of sustainable exclusive control, the potential universality of access, and the precedence of activity over its legal formalization. These principles were expressed in the First Constitution of Space and subsequently applied to digital space without modification.

The present study addresses a different context. Unlike previously considered environments, Earth is traditionally structured through a territorial legal framework based on spatial delimitation and the allocation of jurisdiction. At the same time, as a physical space, Earth exhibits continuity that does not inherently correspond to such divisions.

The paper explores the relationship between these two perspectives and identifies conditions under which tensions arise between the continuous nature of space and its territorial legal organization. Analysis focuses on the limits of their applicability and the extent to which the principles of open environments may be relevant in specific contexts.

It is argued that the model of open environments can be used as an analytical framework for examining situations in which territorial assumptions become less determinative. However, its application to Earth remains context-dependent and limited by the presence of established legal structures.

The study does not seek to provide a definitive conclusion but aims to formulate a set of questions concerning the relationship between spatial continuity and legal organization, thereby outlining directions for further research.

Dapatan ulasan mengenal pasti empat tema utama (1) krisis keahlian dan kepelbagaian tenaga kerja, (2) peralihan daripada kolektivisme kepada individualisme tempat kerja, (3) keperluan transformasi perundangan buruh, dan (4) strategi hibrid kesatuan melalui advokasi digital.Analisis menunjukkan bahawa di Malaysia, khususnya dalam sektor perkhidmatan yang berkembang pesat, kesatuan sekerja menghadapi kekangan struktural namun berpotensi sebagai ejen perlindungan sosial dalam ekonomi gig. Artikel ini menyumbang kepada bidang hubungan pekerjaan melalui pembinaan kerangka konseptual yang mengintegrasikan peranan institusi dengan keperluan perlindungan buruh era baharu. Implikasi kajian mencadangkan perlunya reformasi dasar untuk meningkatkan daya tawar kolektif dalam ekosistem kerja yang semakin tidak formal.

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the National Science Foundation of China (Grants 72272014, Grants 72301031), BIT Science and Technology Innovation Plan "BIT Think Tank" Advancement Program (2025CX13008).

detail.abstract: This paper studies operational planning in centralized charging and decentralized swapping systems under uncertainty. We consider a two-stage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model in which ordering decisions are subject to temporally correlated disruptions, while demand remains stochastic and distributionally ambiguous. To capture this structure, we develop a scenario-wise ambiguity set to describe the disruption and demand uncertainty. Specifically, the disruption process is modeled through a marginal ambiguity set, and the associated worst-case disruption scenarios are characterized by exploiting the supermodularity of the second-stage value function. Conditional on each disruption scenario, demand uncertainty is modeled via a Gelbrich metric ambiguity set, which captures joint mean and covariance information and enables a closed-form reformulation of the resulting distributionally robust chance constraints. The proposed worstcase reliable operation model is tractable and can be easily solved by commercial solvers. Numerical results show that the proposed model outperforms deterministic, stochastic programming, and moment-based DRO benchmarks in both cost and service performance. It further reveals endogenous differentiation in replenishment strategies across stations with heterogeneous capacities. Out-of-sample tests show that the proposed model achieves lower and more stable costs, particularly under high disruption risk and demand variability. These results demonstrate the model's ability to effectively hedge against joint uncertainty while maintaining operational efficiency.

title: A CFAR-based Annotation Framework for Automatic Fall Detection using CNN-BiLSTM on Wearable Inertial Sensor Data
affiliations: University of New South Wales, University of New South Wales (UNSW) and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A CFAR-based Annotation Framework for Automatic Fall Detection using CNN-BiLSTM on Wearable Inertial Sensor Data
detail.abstract: Fall detection is critical for ensuring personnel safety in high-risk environments such as underground mining; however, the performance of deep learning models is often constrained by imprecise temporal labeling and inherent class imbalance. This study proposes a robust detection framework utilizing a CNN-BiLSTM architecture designed to extract integrated spatial and bidirectional temporal features from wearable inertial data. To address the limitations of manual annotation, an automated labeling framework based on the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) algorithm was developed. Statistical validation demonstrates that this autonomous data annotation approach maintains high temporal integrity, yielding a significantly higher Pearson correlation coefficient compared to the benchmark method used in FallNet. The proposed CNN-BiLSTM framework was rigorously evaluated on the KFall and SisFall datasets, covering both pre-impact and post-fall monitoring phases. A comparative analysis of a majority rule versus a 10% ratio rule was conducted across varying sliding windows. For pre-impact detection, the results indicate that the majority rule achieves optimal performance within a shorter 1.5 s interval, whereas the 10% ratio rule performs best as the window extends to 2.0 s. In post-fall detection scenarios, the optimal observation windows for both strategies extend to 2.5 s and 3.0 s, respectively, to capture more continuous fall signatures. Across all configurations, the CNN-BiLSTM variants consistently outperform FallNet and CLSTM benchmarks. This synergy of CFAR-based annotation, adaptive windowing, and hybrid deep learning provides a scalable, high-precision solution for industrial safety surveillance where manual labeling is impractical.
